$comment: Items carry a usage log — `kind: "use"` beats record where and when the thing is actually used, each gated on its own. Written from inside the crawl: what the object is, what it does, what happened when someone used it.

entities.name: The Gate of the Feral Gods
entities.tagline: The Gate of the Feral Gods is said to be buried in the long-lost Necropolis of Anser. A bugbear submarine captain spent close to twenty years looking for it, and an artifact of this grade has no business turning up this early.

description.text: New Quest. The Gate of the Feral Gods. Henrik the Changeling. Commandant Kane. The Mad Dune Mage. They all have pieces of the artifact. Take it from them. Collect all three. Put them together. What happens next is pretty damn neat. Reward: Oh boy-oh-boy.

beats.headline: Hidden in the tomb
beats.text: Carl learns of it from the description of Ruckus, out in the desert quadrant. It lies buried in the Necropolis of Anser, and it has drawn treasure hunters: the bugbear submarine captain Shamus Chaindrive, who spent close to twenty years looking for the tomb, a young mage trying to burrow into it by magic, and a colony of dirigible gnomes. An artifact of this grade has no business appearing before the eighth or ninth floor, and the world freezes for half a second while the game reconciles the conflict.
beats.gist: Carl learns of the Gate of the Feral Gods, a legendary celestial artifact buried in Anser.

beats.headline: Three pieces, three holders
beats.text: A winding box and two magically linked pocket watches. Henrik the Changeling has one watch, the gnomish Commandant Kane the other, and the Mad Dune Mage the box. The quest to collect all three offers a reward of "Oh boy-oh-boy."
beats.gist: The Gate of the Feral Gods consists of a winding box and two magically linked pocket watches.

beats.headline: How to work it
beats.text: Dial a time standing for a place on one watch and the other mirrors it. Both go in the box, which winds and must not be moved or the count resets. Pulling the watches out opens a one-way portal, good for roughly twenty minutes. Afterwards it lingers where it was opened as a two-way passage into the Nothing until something comes through — often a feral god. A weak constitution too near an open portal gets painted with the feral madness.
beats.gist: The Gate of the Feral Gods opens a portal using two watches and a box.

beats.headline: Out of Lusca, and an ocean with it
beats.text: Carl, Katia and Tran kill Lusca and her babies at the bottom of the water quadrant. Carl opens the Gate and takes the three of them to the surface outside the pazuzu town of Pandinus. A spray of ocean comes through in the few seconds the portal is open and knocks over the town wall and a guard tower. A feral god is loose, and the System's achievement warns that other gods tend to react.
beats.gist: Carl, Katia and Tran kill Lusca and her babies; Carl opens the Gate to Pandinus.

beats.headline: A gate to the ninth floor
beats.text: The mage's notes list times standing for places, all of them around the city of Larracos. Katia works out it could open onto the ninth floor — and Mordecai points out that crawlers cannot hop floors, so all that would accomplish is releasing whatever awful thing comes through when it shuts.
beats.gist: Katia identifies the Gate of the Feral Gods as a portal to the ninth floor.

beats.headline: Locked, then released
beats.text: The moment Carl takes Henrik's body into his inventory, and the watch with it, the world freezes. An admin notice flashes past: three items are under an administrative lock while an appeal in the Syndicate court decides whether they are eligible. A second notice follows before the first has finished: lack of standing for all plaintiffs, lock removed, apologies for the inconvenience. Several someones would like the three pieces out of his hands. For now, they have lost.
beats.gist: Carl takes Henrik's body and watch into his inventory, freezing the world and triggering administrative locks.

beats.headline: Seven factions sue, and lose
beats.text: Seven of the faction-wars factions take Carl and the AI to Syndicate court to stop what he means to do with it, and lose. Carl collects seven Fight the Power achievements, and each of the seven Summary Judgement boxes pays out a gold piece, one share of stock and a photograph of a plaintiff's mother.
beats.gist: Seven factions sue Carl and the AI in Syndicate court and lose.

beats.headline: Phase one, one bubble at a time
beats.text: The procedure. A bubble's survivors gather outside their own Desperado Club entrance. One of them goes in, takes the three pieces, comes out and dials the coordinates Katia has worked out; at these distances the portal opens in under a minute. Everyone steps through to Hump Town. The gatekeeper goes last, the gate closes, and a feral god appears in the bubble they have left. The gatekeeper goes back into the club and hands the pieces to the next in line. The first group comes through crying, they are so happy.
beats.gist: Survivors gather at the Desperado Club, use the Gate to reach Hump Town, and leave a feral god.

beats.headline: Phase two, and what got out
beats.text: Phase two runs the same way, on worlds less sure their other quadrants are empty, plus a few added late. By the end of it, about 1,500 crawlers are out. One feral too big for its bubble simply burst, and the bubble opened and poured the gore into the lacuna. Only two got loose out there: a turkey the size of Orthrus and a city-sized swarm of insects. Phase one called three deities and phase two five more; they did damage and went away. The gate comes back to Katia. Nobody tries to steal it.
beats.gist: Phase two leaves 1,500 crawlers out and releases a turkey the size of Orthrus and insects.

beats.headline: Larracos: water, charges and sharks
beats.text: The announced plan was to open onto the Skull Empire army and put a feral god in the middle of it — the exact outcome the lawsuit was meant to prevent. It was cover, planned for days. The winding box Chris throws is a fake; the real gate is with Katia in the water quadrant, and it floods the faction market instead: ocean water, timed explosives and a frenzy of sharks, cutting the factions off from resupply. Carl keeps the artifact rather than spending it. Juice Box goes through with the water.
beats.gist: Carl keeps the Gate of the Feral Gods artifact while Juice Box goes through with the water.

beats.headline: Traded at the Midnight Market
beats.text: Fopsy, the Dream's adjutant, reads it off his menus while Victory swears beside him. The war mages did not keep the Gate of the Feral Gods. They traded it to a minion at the Midnight Market, in exchange for five hell-kissed conscription potions, level 18, strong enough to take most gods, though not sponsored ones. That explains why Eris's pilot had to be ejected first. Victory's observation is that such things always leak into the market. The Gate, as of now, is somewhere else.
beats.gist: Fopsy reads that war mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods for five conscription potions.

beats.headline: Out of the Midnight Market
beats.text: Eris told Carl the War Mages had traded it at the Midnight Market to a merchant named Paca, an agent for Krakaren Prime, who was keeping it in her stomach. Carl passed that on to Justice Light, who knew Paca and knew the market, and went off with his sluggalos. Now, in the middle of everything else, he reports in chat that the Gate of the Feral Gods is retrieved and back at his location. Juice Box, it is ready.
beats.gist: Justice Light retrieves the Gate of the Feral Gods from Paca's stomach and reports it ready.

beats.headline: A portal into the Nothing
beats.text: Its winding box, broken and blood-soaked, has become a permanent portal into the Nothing, and Juice Box has used it to leave the ninth floor. Justice Light, who told her he was going with her and lied, stays on this side to spring the small trap set above it. One snapped piece of twine, and a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap fall into the open portal, carrying the thousands of threads that tie the fairies to the twelfth floor and the thousands of evicted demons.
beats.gist: Juice Box uses the blood-soaked Gate of the Feral Gods to leave the ninth floor.

recap.text: Carl finds the Gate of the Feral Gods, consisting of a winding box and two pocket watches, in the Necropolis of Anser. He uses the artifact to move 1,500 crawlers to Hump Town, leaving feral gods behind in their bubbles. Carl then floods the faction market with ocean water, timed explosives, and sharks.

War mages trade the Gate of the Feral Gods at the Midnight Market for five level 18 hell-kissed conscription potions. Justice Light retrieves the Gate from the stomach of a merchant named Paca using his sluggalos. Juice Box uses the blood-soaked box as a portal into the Nothing to leave the ninth floor. Justice Light snaps twine to drop a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap into the portal.

entities.name: Carl's Doomsday Scenario
entities.tagline: Carl's Doomsday Scenario is a soul crystal going off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, big enough to flatten forty-five square kilometres. It can no longer be stabilized, and it will explode the instant it leaves his inventory.
entities.description: Carl's Doomsday Scenario. Type: Unstable custom explosive. Effect: An explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god. Status: Explosion Imminent. Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders, this device is powerful enough to level an entire city and all the suburbs around it. It is created by combining a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case. Warning: This item can no longer be stabilized.

beats.headline: Built in the middle of a collapse
beats.text: During the Fools Who Broke the Glass, Carl drops a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around a Soul Crystal that is already going up and pulls the result into his inventory. Status: Explosion Imminent. "This item can no longer be stabilized."
beats.gist: Carl drops a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around a rising Soul Crystal and inventories the result.

beats.headline: Forty-five square kilometres
beats.text: Enough to take a city and every suburb around it. It can no longer be stabilized, and the moment it leaves his inventory it goes off, with less than a second to spare. "Created by a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders."
beats.gist: An unstable custom explosive can destroy a city and its suburbs once it leaves Carl's inventory.

beats.headline: On the bench
beats.text: The Advanced Bomber's Studio has a workbench built for examining and dissecting explosives, and Carl sets the Doomsday Scenario on it: the first time he has taken it out of his inventory since he grabbed it. The bench reshapes itself around the glass reaper case, which glows like a miniature sun. It is a microsecond from exploding and there is nothing he can do to stop that. He can copy it into the studio's simulator, where it can be played with safely, and he does. Then it goes back into his inventory, his hands still trembling.
beats.gist: Carl sets the Doomsday Scenario on a workbench in the Advanced Bomber's Studio and copies it.

recap.text: During the Fools Who Broke the Glass, Carl drops a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around a Soul Crystal and pulls the result into his inventory. The item is an unstable custom explosive that cannot be stabilized and will detonate less than a second after leaving his inventory. It can destroy a city and every suburb around it.

Carl sets the Doomsday Scenario on a workbench in the Advanced Bomber's Studio. The bench reshapes itself around the glass reaper case, which glows like a miniature sun. Carl copies the explosive into a simulator before it explodes and puts it back in his inventory with trembling hands.

entities.name: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore
entities.tagline: The Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore is a tiara with a clouded purple stone at its centre. Putting it on places the wearer permanently in the line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor, and Donut put it on before Mordecai could finish warning her.
entities.description: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore. Who's a dirty girl? You're a dirty girl! This is a Fleeting item! This is a Unique* item! Imbues wearer with +5 Intelligence, grants the user +5 to the Good First Impression Skill. All attacks, including magical attacks, now have a 15% chance to inflict the Sepsis Debuff. Warning! (Seriously though. I'm going to say this again. WARNING! Read this shit before you put it on.) Placing this crown upon your head permanently places you within the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor of the world dungeon. Removing this item will not remove this status. Royal members of the Blood Sultanate will be required to slay the Sultan and all other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth floor. You'll only want to wear this if you're a blood-thirsty, raging psychopath.

beats.headline: Out of the Legendary Quadruped Box
beats.text: Awarded for being the first cat into the dungeon. A deep purple stone at the centre, clouded and swirling as though it were liquid. +5 Intelligence, +5 Good First Impression, and a 15% chance for any attack to inflict Sepsis. Donut puts it on while Mordecai is still in the middle of warning her.
beats.gist: Donut puts on the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore while Mordecai is warning her.

beats.headline: The part she skipped
beats.text: "Warning! (Seriously though. I'm going to say this again. WARNING! Read this shit before you put it on.) Placing this crown upon your head permanently places you within the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor of the world dungeon. Removing this item will not remove this status. Royal members of the Blood Sultanate will be required to slay the Sultan and all other members of the royal family before descending to the tenth floor. You'll only want to wear this if you're a blood-thirsty, raging psychopath."
beats.gist: Wearing the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore permanently places the wearer in the Blood Sultanate succession.

beats.headline: Thirty steps
beats.text: The crown's fifteen per cent rides on every missile the cat fires. Every so often a Scatterer takes one to the face and comes away with Sepsis, and when that happens it turns and runs. It usually gets about thirty steps before it collapses, dead. The bad llama wore a debuff called Septic, pulsing over its ruined face: quicker than poison, unstackable, and cured by a simple healing spell or potion.
beats.gist: The crown adds fifteen per cent to missiles the cat fires, killing Scatterers in thirty steps.

beats.headline: Destroyed, and it changes nothing
beats.text: The third pulse of the blast destroys any armour still equipped, and the crown crumbles to dust on her head as she agrees to take it off. The succession is untouched. It said as much on the label.
beats.gist: A blast destroys equipped armour and the crown crumbles to dust; the succession remains untouched.

beats.headline: Binding after it is gone
beats.text: Donut lost the crown at the end of the third floor, and it was regenerated and possibly awarded to someone else. The status stayed with her. Carl knows the description by heart: wearing it places you permanently in the royal line of the Blood Sultanate, and royals must slay the Sultan and every other member of the family before descending to the tenth floor. The royals, he now knows, always make it to the end. Anyone else who put the crown on would have to die too.
beats.gist: Donut lost the Sepsis Crown, but the binding stayed and requires slaying the Blood Sultanate.

beats.headline: It finds its way to Katia
beats.text: Donut lost the crown at the end of the third floor, and it found its way to Eva, fixed to the back shoulder of her glittering breastplate where it passed for decoration. As Katia's sword goes through her, Eva pulls it free with her lower left hand, and from her hand it goes to Katia's head. The hat the Apothecary sent Katia would have stopped it. She gave that to Carl. The crown melds into her form and disappears from sight.
beats.gist: Donut loses the Sepsis Crown, which attaches to Eva's glittering breastplate before melding into Katia's head.

beats.headline: The Sultanate is on this floor
beats.text: The stairs to the tenth do not open for a royal who has not killed the Sultan and the rest of the family.
beats.gist: The stairs to the tenth do not open for a royal who has not killed the Sultan.

recap.text: Donut receives the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore for being the first cat into the dungeon. The crown has a swirling purple stone and gives +5 Intelligence, +5 Good First Impression, and a 15% chance to inflict Sepsis. Donut puts it on before Mordecai warns her that she must slay the Sultan and all other royal family members. A bad llama takes a hit and collapses dead after thirty steps.
The third pulse of a blast destroys any equipped armour. The crown crumbles to dust on her head as she agrees to take it off. The label says the succession is untouched.

Donut loses the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore at the end of the third floor, but the status stays with her. The crown finds its way to Eva, who wears it on the back shoulder of a glittering breastplate. Katia kills Eva with a sword, and the crown moves from Eva's lower left hand to Katia's head. It melds into Katia's form and disappears from sight.
The stairs to the tenth do not open for a royal who has not killed the Sultan and the rest of the family.

entities.name: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook

tagline.text: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook came off a prize carousel looking like a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes, each with a story from its anonymous author.
The Cookbook has been passed from crawl to crawl since the fifteenth season. Carl holds the twenty-fourth edition, and whatever he writes in it goes into the twenty-fifth.

entities.description: Book. The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook by Anonymous. This is a unique item. Chicken and Goblin recipes galore! But it's more than that, too. Each recipe is accompanied by a hilarious tale by the anonymous author, recounting some of the zany and madcap misadventures they experienced gathering these mouth-watering recipes. Fun for the whole family! This book is a real hoot.

beats.headline: Introduced in the Iron Tangle
beats.text: Carl picks it off Chaco's prize carousel as a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes, and it is not new: this is the twenty-fourth edition, first generated in the fifteenth season, and it has been passed from crawl to crawl, each owner adding a page for the next.
beats.gist: Carl picks the twenty-fourth edition of the Cookbook off Chaco's prize carousel as a joke book.

beats.headline: Forkith, for Barkith
beats.text: The bomb-making chapter keeps a thread of notes on madness satchels. Rosetta, ninth edition, found that an equipped backpack stopped them destabilising. Allister, thirteenth, notes the inventory delay she was working around is gone, though backpacks still hold. Forkith, twentieth edition, writes that they only slow it now; he found that out the hard way, and he asks whoever reads it to kill an enemy today in honor of his sister, Barkith, who was all he had left. What Carl takes from all of it is that backpacks are a thing.
beats.gist: The Cookbook notes that backpacks slow madness satchels, and Carl concludes backpacks are a thing.

beats.headline: Some NPCs come back
beats.text: A passage in the NPC chapter, from Crawler Azin of the seventeenth edition: some NPCs are indestructible and regenerate minutes after they are killed, which means they carry or know something big. A note from the twenty-second edition adds a story of tying one to the front of a shield, which the Nagas quietly patched the next day, and of a man who exploded and was reborn each time he was dragged out of his church. He knew the password to the safe holding the stairwell key. Carl remembers it at the Downward Dog, listening to a gnoll whose throat was ripped out.
beats.gist: Crawler Azin writes that indestructible NPCs regenerate and hold big information. Carl remembers this at the Downward Dog.

beats.headline: Three kinds of summoning
beats.text: Deities get no chapter of their own, only notes in the miscellaneous one. Coolie, nineteenth edition: there are three kinds of summoning, the celestial boon, the indentured and the involuntary, which arrives untethered and smashes everything, and in Coolie's experience all three end with the summoner dead. Gods are invulnerable below the twelfth floor. Forkith, twentieth, adds that they still bleed, and prays to reach the twelfth to kill one for a sister, Barkith. Tin, twenty-first: gods are Soul Armor, worn by aliens like clothes, so a spell that strips biological armour could in theory strip the driver.
beats.gist: The Cookbook describes three types of summoning that kill the summoner and how to strip gods.

beats.headline: Keep it away from the market
beats.text: The new marketplace interface would finally put a price on everything in Carl's inventory, and the Cookbook warns against using it while carrying the Cookbook. Batbilge, twelfth edition, found the market values the tome as a unique heirloom at something like fifty million gold, and did not like giving a third party that kind of look into his inventory. Allister, thirteenth edition, added that this appears to be Batbilge's last entry, and that he leaves his cards on his bed whenever he trades. For Allister it took the form of a deck of cards. Carl plans to use his bedside table.
beats.gist: The Cookbook warns against using the marketplace interface while carrying the tome.

beats.headline: Coolie's last notes, and Carl's first
beats.text: Three notes by Crawler Coolie, nineteenth edition, run through the pages: a program on a ship in low orbit, its open window held by a forcefield; bugbear paste in his boots for the two admins on his next show; then failure. The admins were holos, the forcefield kept the ship whole, and he wrote as the air thinned, looking down at his planet, Qurux. Beneath them now sits a note from Crawler Carl, twenty-fifth edition: Coolie's passage helped plan the first step, and it was done for him and for a little girl named Bonnie. Then a second note, one word long. One.
beats.gist: Crawler Coolie writes of a ship in low orbit, bugbear paste in boots, and the planet Qurux.

beats.headline: Sinjin on worshipping a god
beats.text: Sinjin, fifteenth edition, worshipped the goddess Kuraokami and called it the worst decision ever. The rules: touch every kill with ice once a day. Five days running earns a boon. Miss one and she turns her back; miss two, a debuff; miss three and you fall from grace, with a fifty-fifty chance of being smote. Leaving voluntarily is an automatic smite. Her sponsor messaged him constantly. Then a note from Azin, seventeenth edition: that was Sinjin's last entry, a man in Azin's party had a blindness debuff made permanent by his god, and the advice is to stay away from gods.
beats.gist: Sinjin worshipped Kuraokami, but Azin advises staying away from gods.

beats.headline: The aerosol, disguised as smoke
beats.text: Carl needs Mordecai's weedkiller turned into a mist over a monster's head, and the cookbook has a bomb built for exactly that. He does not build the cookbook's version, which is smaller and stronger and would be impossible to explain. He builds a clumsier one out of modified hobgoblin smoke curtains and tells Mordecai he worked it out himself in three tries. Stripped of its charge, the device no longer counts as an explosive, so his throwing arm gets no help with it.
beats.gist: Carl builds a clumsy bomb from modified hobgoblin smoke curtains to mist weedkiller over a monster.

beats.headline: Ikicha's last entry
beats.text: Ikicha wrote of seeing someone he loved, twisted and changed, speaking in the same voice, and told the next reader not to try: hope is crucial, but blind hope is poison. Drakea's note under it says it took a while to understand him. Gone is gone. Everything else is puppets built by the enemy. And yet she dreams of a fire across the sky. For you, Ikicha. Carl read it a while ago. With Ferdinand on a rhinoceros, he cannot stop thinking about it.
beats.gist: Ikicha writes that blind hope is poison; Drakea notes that gone is gone.

beats.headline: Milk on the Treasure Map
beats.text: Crawler Milk's note in the sixth edition: when a country boss dies, it drops persistent loot called the Treasure Map. Don't pick it up. Over four hundred crawlers faced a boss in a low-ceilinged cave and fewer than fifty survived, hitting each other as often as it. Then they all picked up the map, which showed every piece of magical gear in the area, and started a second slaughter. Milk's first player-killer skull came from it. Blood on the claws, the note says, that will not wash away.
beats.gist: Crawler Milk writes that picking up a country boss's Treasure Map causes a second slaughter.

beats.headline: He writes his own plan into it
beats.text: Alongside a copy of the notes the team has been passing through the Coffee Shop Author's Kit, a way of talking that prying eyes cannot see. Goal one: survive the Butcher's Masquerade, which he calls a trap. Everything else is secondary.
beats.gist: Carl writes a plan into the Cookbook using the Coffee Shop Author's Kit to survive the Butcher's Masquerade.

beats.headline: Everly takes it all back
beats.text: Three entries from Crawler Everly. First: a sponsor box meant for one of her mercenaries, a spellbook he used within five hours to kill the boss holding the lockbox key. She does not trust sponsors, she writes, but they want her alive. Second, on floor eight, a tool for shortcuts through the maze, and a spark of hope. Third: I take it back. I take it all back. The sponsor was steering her toward a death that would be watched and remembered. Drakea notes it is her last entry, and asks the next author for detail.
beats.gist: Everly writes three entries about sponsor boxes before Drakea notes it is her last entry.

beats.headline: T'Ghee, by Allister's account
beats.text: The announcement mentions T'Ghee totems, and Carl's breath catches, because he already knows the word. Allister, who wrote the thirteenth edition, treated T'Ghee as a religion, with nothing to do with capturing or summoning monsters. Carl can already see how the dungeon means to use it anyway. Mordecai supplies the dungeon's version: large playing cards, like Bautista's stuffed animals or Carl's tarot cards, reusable even when the summoned monster dies.
beats.gist: An announcement mentions T'Ghee totems, which Allister wrote about as a religion in the thirteenth edition.

beats.headline: Rosetta on fairies
beats.text: A note in the ninth edition, in Rosetta's hand: fairies and sprites look fragile and are not. They are fast, magical and always alert, and their luck is unnatural; something crazy always happens when she tries to fight one. If you must, pull their wings off. They come off easily, and that is where they keep their magic. Carl takes the warning about luck to heart the day he and Katia mean to kill a fairy. The claymores alone should do it; he adds the teleport traps, and Katia with her deck, anyway.
beats.gist: Rosetta writes that fairies are fast, alert, and have unnatural luck; Carl uses claymores and traps.

beats.headline: The third edition's author
beats.text: Dante, a crocodilian thief, wrote the third edition, and only a single entry of it, afraid of being caught. He took a deal at the start of the eleventh floor and worked as a game guide, then moved to the Trap Master guild to be near his skyfowl neighbour, a shopkeeper who had also owned the Cookbook. He never told him who he was. Reassigned with that neighbour as a castle guard for one season's eighth floor, fourteen seasons short of freedom, he refused to follow orders. Administrative action killed him.
beats.gist: Dante, a crocodilian thief, wrote one entry of the third edition of the Cookbook.

beats.headline: The fourth edition's author
beats.text: Tipid, a Crest poisoner, wrote the fourth edition. He got out at the start of the twelfth floor with a key that let only one of them through a door, and he chose himself over his friend Horatio. He had negotiated an extra season to keep that key; he tore it off its chain and threw it across the table. Damage to his brain took his whole pension and a loan to repair. He settled in a Crest system and worked for a waste management company. Current status: Colonel in the Princess Posse.
beats.gist: Tipid, a Crest poisoner, wrote the fourth edition of the Cookbook.

beats.headline: The fifth author, in a tower
beats.text: Everly, a sward mantis who crawled alone with hired mercenaries, gets a compass from her sponsor that shows the safest path through a fifty-level tower. It has forty-nine uses. At the top, a note: the tower is an advertisement, the compass named for a competitor, the dead end sponsored by the very company that sent it. She scrawls an angry note in the cookbook as the roof starts to come down. Explosives Engineer. Primal. Crushed to death on the eighth floor. Author of the fifth edition.
beats.gist: Everly, a sward mantis and Primal Explosives Engineer, writes the fifth edition of the cookbook.

beats.headline: The seventh edition's only entry
beats.text: The seventh edition's author was a pet bird named Volteeg who took the biscuit, became a gargoyle on the third floor, and could never sing properly again. His owner died on the seventh. The Cookbook came to him then, and he did nothing with it, until the very end of the ninth, when he wrote his one and only entry. Now he is back as a Weeper commander for the Operatic Collective. He pulls out his tank's fire-control chamber, fills the tank with energy balls, drives it toward the warlord Hortense's caravan and lights a blitz stick. Over ten thousand die.
beats.gist: Volteeg writes one entry in the Cookbook and kills ten thousand people with a tank.

beats.headline: A note on first worship
beats.text: Crawler Carl adds a note in the twenty-fifth edition, on things Rosetta, Tipid and Justice Light tell him. When someone worships a god for the first time, a tiny non-corporeal fairy mob called a Bijou drags a whisker-thin tendril of invisible light from the god to the strongest temple on the floor, and from the temple to the new adherent's heart. It takes about two minutes. From the third floor to the eleventh, the strongest temple is almost always inside Club Vanquisher. Nobody has ever caught a Bijou, though Mordecai thinks the right trap might. Edgar's Sense Movement can see them rise.
beats.gist: Carl adds a note to the twenty-fifth edition of the Cookbook about first worship.

beats.headline: The tenth edition's author
beats.text: Its tenth edition was written by York, a tenodera Advocate who reached level 71, took a deal at the end of the tenth floor, and worked as a game guide and a guildhall instructor in the Poetry guild. He now flies Homecoming Queen alone in orbit and writes poems he suspects are terrible. Rosetta asked whether he could destroy an orc yacht full of children, the new king of the orcs among them. He could. He wanted to feel something afterwards. He feels something only when Boomer says it is time to bring the war out of the dungeon.
beats.gist: York wrote the tenth edition of the Cookbook.

recap.text: Carl picks the Cookbook off Chaco's prize carousel as a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes. Forkith, twentieth edition, writes that madness satchels only slow down in backpacks and asks the reader to kill an enemy for his sister, Barkith. Crawler Azin of the seventeenth edition notes that some indestructible NPCs regenerate and know something big. Tin, twenty-first edition, writes that gods are Soul Armor worn by aliens.

The Cookbook warns Carl against using the marketplace interface because Batbilge found the tome is valued at fifty million gold. Crawler Coolie wrote of bugbear paste in boots and a ship in orbit over Qurux before he failed. Carl writes a note for Coolie and a girl named Bonnie. Sinjin worshipped Kuraokami by touching kills with ice, but Azin warns to stay away from gods.

Carl builds a clumsy bomb from hobgoblin smoke curtains to mist weedkiller over a monster, lying to Mordecai that it took three tries. He reads notes from Ikicha and Drakea about puppets built by the enemy and a warning from Crawler Milk that a Treasure Map causes slaughters. Carl uses a Coffee Shop Author's Kit to plan survival for the Butcher's Masquerade. Crawler Everly writes three entries before claiming a sponsor steered her toward a watched death.

Carl recognizes T'Ghee from Allister's thirteenth edition, where it is a religion. Mordecai explains the dungeon uses T'Ghee as reusable playing cards to summon monsters. Rosetta's note in the ninth edition warns that fairies have unnatural luck and magic in their wings. Carl and Katia use claymores, teleport traps, and a deck to kill a fairy.

Dante wrote one entry of the third edition and administrative action killed him. Tipid wrote the fourth edition and became a Colonel in the Princess Posse. Everly wrote the fifth edition and was crushed to death on the eighth floor. Volteeg wrote the seventh edition. He drove a tank into Hortense's caravan and ten thousand died. Carl adds a note to the twenty-fifth edition. York wrote the tenth edition and flies Homecoming Queen in orbit.

entities.name: Enhanced Pet Biscuit
entities.tagline: An Enhanced Pet Biscuit has over a hundred possible effects, half of them good and the rest neutral or worse. The cat snatched this one out of Carl's hand, melted into a heap of furry goo, and got up talking.
entities.description: Enhanced Pet Biscuit. So, it looks like a regular pet biscuit. It's not. Feed to your pet at your own risk. What's the worst that can happen?

beats.headline: She takes it out of his hand
beats.text: It comes out of the Legendary Pet Box awarded for being the first crawler to bring a cat down the stairs. She snatches it, melts into a heap of furry goo, and gets up talking.
beats.gist: Donut snatches an Enhanced Pet Biscuit from a Legendary Pet Box and talks after melting into goo.

beats.headline: A biscuit per cage
beats.text: In the kobold fighting pits, a single biscuit tossed into a beaten danger dingo's cage turns its dot from red to white. Carl does it for all fourteen, over the cat's objection that it is her food. When a dying kobold opens the cages, the dingoes turn on their masters instead of on the crawlers, and the first one fed swallows the neighbourhood boss whole. That was the trick of the room.
beats.gist: Carl tosses an Enhanced Pet Biscuit into fourteen danger dingo cages, turning their dots white.

beats.headline: Three biscuits, one herd
beats.text: The recap follows a crawler who entered with fifteen goats and has five left. She fed them three pet biscuits, and the third one went badly for several of the goats. Of the two that changed, one now walks upright in armor with a double-headed axe, screaming occasionally for no reason. The other is a hellspawn familiar: a horse-sized, pitch-black goat with glowing red eyes and six breasts. Mordecai rates hellspawn among the most powerful pets in the game, likely to sprout wings and grow to dragon size if kept alive.
beats.gist: A crawler feeds three pet biscuits to goats, creating an armored goat and a six-breasted hellspawn.

beats.headline: Enriched, with a known result
beats.text: Prepotente puts one on the bar table: an Enriched Pet Biscuit, one of three from a celestial box, and unlike the ordinary sort it leaves nothing to chance. This one is "The Paramour": an upright transformation, a reset to level one, crawler status, and a permanent, incurable charm that makes the eater fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them. Its siblings are "Nothing Special", which makes a plain dungeon pet, and "Nothing Special Party Companion", which keeps the animal's shape and gives it no voice.
beats.gist: Prepotente puts an Enriched Pet Biscuit called The Paramour on the bar table.

beats.headline: The wrong biscuit
beats.text: Prepotente's box held three biscuits. The Nothing Special Party Companion one went into Penelope, who is a crawler now. The plan for Scolopendra was the plain Nothing Special: a regular pet, level 1, to live in a carrier in Carl's inventory as a fail-safe. Searching and combining in Carl's inventory at speed, Donut picked the wrong one, and the dungeon boss comes out of the goo as a crawler instead.
beats.gist: Donut picks the wrong biscuit from Prepotente's box, making the dungeon boss a crawler.

recap.text: A cat snatches a biscuit from a Legendary Pet Box awarded for bringing a cat down the stairs, melts into furry goo, and begins to talk. In the kobold fighting pits, Carl tosses one biscuit into each of fourteen danger dingo cages. The dingoes turn on their masters, and the first one fed swallows the neighbourhood boss whole.

A crawler feeds three pet biscuits to her goats. One goat walks upright in armor with a double-headed axe and screams for no reason. Another becomes a horse-sized, pitch-black hellspawn familiar with glowing red eyes and six breasts. Mordecai says hellspawn may sprout wings and grow to dragon size.

Prepotente has three Enriched Pet Biscuits from a celestial box. The Paramour resets a crawler to level one and makes them fall in love with the feeder, while Nothing Special makes a plain pet and Nothing Special Party Companion keeps the animal's shape without a voice. Donut picks the wrong biscuit from Carl's inventory, and the dungeon boss becomes a crawler.

entities.name: Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering

tagline.text: Frank Q gave Carl this ring as a curse: while one of its marks lives, the wearer cannot be healed. Carl wears it anyway, for the five percent it adds to every stat.
The ring marks a target, and when the target dies, the wearer keeps a point of its best stat. Mordecai says it is addictive, and Donut does not want Carl picking up a new habit.

description.text: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering. Oooh, that's scary sounding. For the discerning Crawler Killer, this magical ring can be one of the most formidable items in the dungeon. If utilized properly, this ring's wielder can grow exponentially in strength, especially on the deeper floors. But beware. If poorly wielded, this ring will kill you quicker than an exploding rage elemental. Either way, this ring imparts one of the dungeon's most highly sought-after skills. The wearer of this ring receives the following benefits: +5% to all stats. The Marked For Death skill.

beats.headline: A curse, handed over at the Desperado Club
beats.text: Frank Q gives it to Carl at the Desperado Club, and it is meant as a curse. He and Maggie My made their daughter Yvette wear one to level up, and Yvette marked Carl before they attacked him on the first floor. A wearer cannot heal while a mark lives, so when Yvette was hurt, Maggie had to kill her own daughter. Carl keeps the ring for the five percent.
beats.gist: Frank Q gives Carl the Ring of Divine Suffering as a curse at the Desperado Club.

beats.headline: Mordecai sees it on his hand
beats.text: Back from his suspension for throwing a chair at Chaco, Mordecai sees the ring on Carl's finger and tells him to get rid of it at once. Carl is wearing it for the five percent to all stats and nothing else. After a smack on the head he pulls it off, agreeing only to talk about selling it before the sixth floor.
beats.gist: Mordecai returns from suspension and tells Carl to remove the Ring of Divine Suffering.

beats.headline: Zockau
beats.text: Carl goes at the hunters with it — marking one, killing him, taking the stat — while his explosives bring the town down around them and trap whoever is inside the Desperado Club. He is badly hurt getting out.
beats.gist: Carl uses the Ring of Divine Suffering to mark and kill a hunter for his stat.

beats.headline: Mordecai's warning
beats.text: Donut passes it on: Mordecai says it is addictive.
beats.gist: Donut says Mordecai warns that the Ring of Divine Suffering is addictive.

beats.headline: A web on the elbow
beats.text: The Gold Junkie's box Carl earned for using the ring the first time opens with nothing in it. A spiderweb pattern appears in the air instead and settles onto his left elbow as a tattoo, faded, green-tinted and poorly drawn: the Night Wyrm's Nasty Little Web of Suffering, which gives its bearer access to a guild. Mordecai says it is a cult, not a real guild and not a real church, worshipping the Night Wyrm, a demigod outside the regular pantheon. Everybody who uses a divine suffering artifact is marked this way.
beats.gist: Carl uses the Ring of Divine Suffering and receives a faded, green-tinted spiderweb tattoo on his elbow.

beats.headline: Two points a kill
beats.text: Congratulations, Murderer. With Akland dead, the ring levels up and now gives two stat points for every kill. This one paid out a single point of constitution, the elf's highest stat, along with two trophies and level 55 for Carl, who had forgotten to summon his gauntlet. The elf's inventory is crawler biscuits and another gonorrhea arrow, obviously meant for Louis. Donut says it was unnecessarily gruesome, that he is getting angrier and angrier and it is scaring her. He promises to kill them nice and clean.
beats.gist: The Ring of Divine Suffering gives Carl two stat points for every kill after Akland dies.

beats.headline: Marking priests mid-brawl
beats.text: Carl picks a nebular priest out of the melee by the Q at the start of his name, finds the only nebular on the ring's list beginning with Q, and marks him just before a berserking mantis cleaves him in half. He marks the next, and the next, and then stops, because they are all fighting and all injured and he does not dare mark more. All three had intelligence as their highest stat. Marked For Death levels between the second and third kill: seven points. Vrah is on the list. Lucia is not.
beats.gist: Carl marks three nebular priests with the Ring of Divine Suffering before a mantis cleaves one.

beats.headline: Two rings, one mark
beats.text: Prepotente had a ring of his own, freshly acquired against Miriam's advice. When his Community Pool spell bounced back and forth between him and Viscount Fog, the magical burst made his items misbehave, and his ring marked the only eligible target in reach, which was Miriam. Left to Fester: while she lives he cannot heal, and he has one point of life. Carl adds a second mark at dawn with his own ring, behind his back, where nobody present can see.
beats.gist: Prepotente marks Miriam with a ring, preventing Fester from healing while he has one life point.

beats.headline: Congratulations, Murderer
beats.text: Carl kills Iota, the drunk hunter teleported into his lap by the new saferoom rules, by crushing his chest with one foot in mid-sentence, after pulling a nipple ring from him with a toe. Iota's highest stat was Intelligence, so the kill pays three points. Then the ring itself levels: Congratulations, Murderer. It now gives four stat points for every kill.
beats.gist: Carl kills Iota by pulling a nipple ring with a toe and crushing his chest.

beats.headline: Marked at full health
beats.text: The ring only marks a target at full health, and Empress D'Nadia keeps herself just short of it on purpose. So the clockwork Mongos go through her shields and the gown, a knife drops, the thing she has been using to keep herself hurt, and when she reaches for it a clockwork snaps the tentacle off. Carl casts a Heal scroll on her. The moment she is whole, he marks her. Her highest stat is Intelligence. The mark will form in thirty seconds.
beats.gist: The ring marks a target at full health, so Carl heals Empress D'Nadia to mark her.

beats.headline: The spare goes to Li Na
beats.text: Carl's spare Night Wyrm's ring now belongs to Li Na. She asked, and his first reaction was no: she might already be the most powerful crawler in the dungeon. He asked Katia, Imani, Donut and Elle privately. Only Imani was against it. Elle was vehement: at least she's our scary psycho. Donut, not using chat, simply said please, Carl, please give it to her, as soon as you can. The brig at the foot of Li Na's clock tower, full of mercenaries nobody trusts, is now empty save the one prisoner Carl asked to be left alone.
beats.gist: Carl gives his spare Ring of Divine Suffering to Li Na.

beats.headline: Every mark, and two missing
beats.text: The ring is why Carl cannot mark anyone in the ball: no simultaneous marks are allowed on this floor, and Li Na has already marked them all. She comes out of the finisher at three hundred across the board. But two notifications that should have come do not. Fang and the Dream's warlord both got away, and while a marked enemy lives, she cannot heal. Every time she uses her chains, she loses a little health.
beats.gist: The Ring of Divine Suffering prevents Carl from marking anyone because Li Na marked them all.

recap.text: Frank Q gives Carl the Ring of Divine Suffering at the Desperado Club as a curse. Maggie My killed her daughter Yvette because a wearer cannot heal while a mark lives. Carl wears the ring for a five percent stat increase. Mordecai returns from a suspension for throwing a chair at Chaco and tells Carl to remove the ring.

Carl uses the ring to kill a hunter and trap others in the Desperado Club. He earns a faded, green-tinted tattoo of the Night Wyrm's Nasty Little Web of Suffering on his left elbow. After killing Akland and Iota, the ring levels up to give four stat points per kill. Carl also marks nebular priests and Miriam.

The ring marks targets at full health, so Carl casts a Heal scroll on Empress D'Nadia to mark her. Carl gives a spare ring to Li Na after Donut asks him to. Li Na marks everyone at the ball, which prevents Carl from marking anyone and stops her from healing while Fang and the Dream's warlord live.

entities.name: Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace
entities.tagline: Eat the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and you spend an hour unconscious at one percent health, with healing blocked. Survive it, and the goddess decides which of her boons you receive.
entities.description: Warning: This item can only be used by a female. Or a male, if you're a seahorse. It's a flower. You're supposed to eat it, though it might be a good decoration instead. […] Anyway, if you eat this flower, it renders you unconscious for one hour with your health at 1% of your max. You cannot heal during this time. If you survive this ordeal, you will be given one of three permanent boons from the goddess Eileithyia. The given boon is at the discretion of the goddess, and it cannot be predicted. If you choose to worship Eileithyia before you consume this flower, the descriptions of the boons will be expanded. She will also ask you which of the three you'd prefer. Her cooperation is not guaranteed, especially if she doesn't like you. But Eileithyia is known to be a generous goddess.

beats.headline: Inside the Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm
beats.text: The system is characteristically unhelpful: "It's a flower. You're supposed to eat it, though it might be a good decoration instead. It probably tastes like a bullshit salad at some hippie vegan restaurant with a month-long waiting list." Eating it means an hour unconscious at 1% health with healing blocked. Survive and Eileithyia grants one of three permanent boons, her choice — unless you worship her first, in which case she expands the descriptions and asks your preference. Her cooperation is not guaranteed.
beats.gist: Carl finds the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace in the Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm.

beats.headline: Katia's way out
beats.text: She takes it and leaves the crawl, human again and missing pieces of herself.
beats.gist: Katia takes the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and leaves the crawl as a human missing pieces.

recap.text: The system describes the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace as a flower that tastes like a bullshit salad at a hippie vegan restaurant. Eating it leaves the user unconscious for an hour at 1% health with healing blocked. Eileithyia grants one of three permanent boons, her choice, unless the user worships her first.
Katia takes the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and leaves the crawl. She is human again and missing pieces of herself.

tagline.text: According to Mordecai, the Guild of Suffering keeps something called a memorial crystal, which is like a soul crystal, except that nobody has ever established what it does.

A memorial crystal is what a fallen god or demigod leaves behind. This one is the most expensive prize on Chaco's counter, at a hundred hunter hands: the queen usually wears it around her neck, and nobody knows which dead god made it.

description.text: Memorial Crystal. Apito. This item is 0% charged.

beats.headline: The queen's prize, at a hundred hands
beats.text: At the end of Chaco's prize case sits a colourless, grape-sized gem that glitters even as a hologram. It is not a soul crystal. It costs a hundred hunter hands, the most expensive thing on the counter. Chaco does not know which dead god made it: the high elves found it on a mining expedition, and the queen normally wears it around her neck. The spell requires the host to offer her most valuable possession as a prize. If nobody buys it, she gets it back.
beats.gist: A colorless, grape-sized gem costs a hundred hunter hands in Chaco's prize case.

beats.headline: Taken off Imogen
beats.text: Someone named Osvaldo takes hers, and Prepotente wants it for a quest.
beats.gist: Osvaldo takes Imogen's Memorial Crystal, and Prepotente wants it for a quest.

beats.headline: It is Apito's
beats.text: Nobody bought it at the counter, so it went back to Imogen, and it came off her body. Prepotente says it is a memorial crystal for the goddess Apito, which should be impossible: as far as anyone knows she is not dead, and she just ran a party. Carl gets a quest update in the voice of Emberus: obtain the item Memorial Crystal: Apito, and see whether it has any bearing on Geyrun's murder.
beats.gist: Imogen loses a crystal for Apito; Emberus quests Carl to check its link to Geyrun's murder.

beats.headline: One made by a god who lives
beats.text: Pater Coal lays the problem out for Carl, on Emberus's behalf. A memorial crystal forms only when a god has died. Apito, the Oak Mother, is alive, and yet there is a crystal made by her. How is that possible? Emberus worries that something may have happened to his mother. The quest to find Geyrun's killer now runs through that crystal: Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet are both named as paths to the answer, and neither can be followed without that memorial crystal.
beats.gist: Pater Coal tells Carl that a memorial crystal exists for the living Oak Mother, Apito.

beats.headline: Round Osvaldo's neck
beats.text: The daily show plays in a small roadside saferoom, where a bopca named Pahzi has served Donut her crab and Carl a pork sandwich. It cuts to Osvaldo in a sprawling city, doing parkour off the walls after a monkey thing swinging along the electrical lines. He is wearing the memorial crystal around his neck.
beats.gist: Pahzi the bopca serves Donut crab and Carl a pork sandwich while Osvaldo wears a memorial crystal.

beats.headline: One for a goddess
beats.text: When Ysalte falls, the world notifications include a Memorial Crystal generated for her, to be available for looting on a future floor, with great riches promised to whoever finds it. The same run of notifications marks her killer for death by every deity except her sworn enemies, and inflicts the Despondent debuff permanently on all of her worshippers.
beats.gist: Ysalte falls, generating a Memorial Crystal for future looting and marking her killer for divine death.

beats.headline: The crystal shows itself
beats.text: A funnel of prismatic light bursts up out of the Madness woods a mile away, bright enough to pierce the clouds, and starts to wave back and forth like somebody shaking a flashlight. The trees grow taller where it falls. Carl's quest updates: Find Out Who Killed My Son. The Memorial Crystal of Apito has just shown itself; abandon the current task and obtain it. It will have to wait. The crawler carrying it, Osvaldo, cannot get it back into his inventory, and Elle points out that every observation spell the enemy has is about to turn this way.
beats.gist: A prismatic light funnel bursts from the Madness woods, and Carl's quest updates to find Apito's crystal.

beats.headline: From Osvaldo to the goat
beats.text: Emberus updates Carl's quest to find who killed his son. Apito's memorial crystal has fallen from Crawler Osvaldo's hands and is now held by Crawler Prepotente, and Carl is to retrieve it before the goat cracks its secrets and hands them to the Epicure. Carl has no idea how it moved without a fight. Osvaldo sits on the ground with his unaffiliated crew, glaring at Prepotente. Carl decides his talk with Prepotente can wait until neither of them is so keyed up.
beats.gist: Emberus tells Carl to retrieve Apito's memorial crystal from Prepotente before the goat hands secrets to the Epicure.

beats.headline: Tupa rejects two of them
beats.text: Osvaldo held two: Apito's, looted as Queen Imogen died, and Ysalte's, hunted down in the Faction Wars forest. His god Tupa called the first corrupted and the second wrong as well. Osvaldo's quest has changed with it: he is now to find out why the memorial crystals are not working right. He gave the first one to Prepotente, who has a quest for it of his own, and Carl has one too.
beats.gist: Tupa rejects two memorial crystals, and Osvaldo must find out why they are not working right.

beats.headline: Zero per cent, and it should not exist
beats.text: Examined by Carl in the pet stables, it reads Memorial Crystal. Apito. 0% charged, and nothing more. It is meant to charge as its bearer kills, and once full to give up the spells, skills and knowledge inside. It never has. It flared into the sky once, near the end of Faction Wars, at the moment Yarilo stepped out of the Nothing, when Apito might have been expected to appear and did not. Carl's patch went off at the same moment, and misfired. Osvaldo holds a second crystal. It will not charge either.
beats.gist: Carl examines a Memorial Crystal in the pet stables that reads Apito and is 0% charged.

beats.headline: A crystal that wants a plinth
beats.text: Crawler Britney drops on Osvaldo moving as fast as he did, because she now carries the memorial crystal from Ysalte. Samantha, suddenly serious, says Britney needs to set it in a plinth in the Basilica or the Vulgar Temple, or, as she also puts it, the Halls of the Ascendency or Sheol, if she wants that crazy Ysalte out of her. Meanwhile Prepotente's Apito crystal has shielded him, Jurgen and their mount from the Transformation, and stands at eleven point one per cent.
beats.gist: Crawler Britney drops on Osvaldo while carrying Ysalte's memorial crystal.

beats.headline: Twenty-two crawlers in one RV
beats.text: The second of the nine attacks, the Sin of Consumption, comes with a thirty percent chance for everyone. Twenty-two crawlers and all their mercenaries are crammed into Makana's RV, with the Apito memorial crystal around Prepotente's neck, and in theory it protects everyone inside. It does. The mounts outside have no such cover: Donut saves Gonk from the worms, and Sweety dies.
beats.gist: Twenty-two crawlers and mercenaries crowd Makana's RV, where Apito's memorial crystal protects them from the Sin of Consumption.

beats.headline: Two of them, at the end
beats.text: Taranis steals Prepotente's. Carl finds another, made by Emberus dying.
beats.gist: Taranis steals Prepotente's Memorial Crystal, and Carl finds one made by Emberus dying.

recap.text: A grape-sized, colourless gem sits in Chaco's prize case costing a hundred hunter hands. The high elves found it on a mining expedition for the queen. Imogen gets it back when nobody buys it. Prepotente says it is a memorial crystal for the goddess Apito. Emberus gives Carl a quest to obtain the crystal to see if it relates to Geyrun's murder.

Pater Coal tells Carl that Apito is alive, yet a memorial crystal exists for her. Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet require this crystal to find Geyrun's killer. Osvaldo wears the crystal around his neck while doing parkour in a city. When Ysalte falls, a notification announces a memorial crystal for her and the Despondent debuff for her worshippers.

A funnel of prismatic light bursts out of the Madness woods and waves like a flashlight. The Memorial Crystal of Apito falls from Crawler Osvaldo's hands into the hands of Crawler Prepotente. Carl's quest updates to find who killed his son and retrieve the crystal before the goat hands its secrets to the Epicure. Osvaldo sits on the ground and glares at Prepotente.

Osvaldo holds memorial crystals for Apito and Ysalte, but Tupa rejects both. Carl's Apito crystal stays at zero per cent and misfired when Yarilo stepped out of the Nothing. Prepotente's Apito crystal protects twenty-two crawlers in Makana's RV from the Sin of Consumption, though Sweety dies. Taranis steals Prepotente's crystal, and Carl finds one made by Emberus dying.

entities.name: Tiara of a Thousand Lights
entities.tagline: The Tiara of a Thousand Lights came out of a celestial box from a waste-management company, on the eve of a war. Donut wears it with Quan Ch's cloak, though nothing has been charged into it yet.

description.text: The Tiara of a Thousand Lights and Accompanying Charge Pillow. This is a unique item. This item was made especially for Crawler Princess Donut by her sponsor, Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions. […] This particular tiara is imbued with 99 Absorption Jewels. The tiara itself has no inherent magical properties, and in its base state it gives no additional benefits or buffs except plus 10 to Charisma. However, it has the ability to be permanently charged with up to 99 different buff items. […] With some careful planning, one can turn this tiara into one of the most powerful items in the history of Dungeon Crawler World. Okay, here come the warnings.

beats.headline: Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions
beats.text: Donut's celestial box from the sponsor holds it. She puts on Quan Ch's cloak in the same stretch and wears the two together, though nothing is charged into the tiara yet.
beats.gist: Donut takes the Tiara of a Thousand Lights from a celestial box and wears Quan Ch's cloak.

beats.headline: Twenty-three, seventy-six to go
beats.text: Katia works through Donut's hats on the charging pillows. Two drained hats come off and the tiara goes onto each pillow in turn: three more absorption jewels light, twenty-three sparkling in all, seventy-six to go. Plus ten to Constitution, plus two to Dodge, which should bring it to fifteen, and a one percent Intelligence buff that wastes a crystal but came on the same hat as the Dodge. Next on the pillow is a plastic baseball cap Carl has never seen before, which is supposed to give her Steady.
beats.gist: Katia uses charging pillows to light twenty-three jewels on the Tiara of a Thousand Lights.

recap.text: Donut takes the Tiara of a Thousand Lights from a celestial box and wears it with Quan Ch's cloak. Katia places the tiara on charging pillows with Donut's hats. Twenty-three absorption jewels light, adding ten to Constitution, two to Dodge, and a one percent Intelligence buff. Katia then places a plastic baseball cap on the pillow to give Donut Steady.

tagline.text: The Scavenger's Daughter is a divine back patch for Carl's jacket: a pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat. What it does depends on which gods, and certain demons, happen to be nearby.
The Scavenger's Daughter is also a person. The war mages came to the castle looking for her, found her, and have left with her.

description.text: The Scavenger's Daughter. Upgrade Patch. Back Patch. This is a divine item. This is a unique item. This is a fleeting item. You may only affix one back patch at a time. This patch depicts a pile of scary skulls, all stacked up nice and neat. I wonder if there's a story there? If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: (Hidden until it is affixed and then worn.) […] Warning #2! This is a divine item. This means it gains differing abilities, buffs, and possibly debuffs depending on your proximity to certain deities and demons. It makes for new and exciting combinations!

beats.headline: A pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat
beats.text: Out of the celestial predator box, opened in the same haul as a prison tattoo kit and a crafting table kit: a divine back patch for Carl's jacket, its benefits varying with whichever deities and certain demons happen to be near. The upgrades it carries stay hidden until it is affixed and worn.
beats.gist: Carl opens a celestial predator box for a divine back patch, tattoo kit, and crafting table kit.

beats.headline: The Daughter's Kiss
beats.text: About ten duende kills fill the essence bar to the top, a sickly brown swirled with yellow and green, like sewage with oil spilled in it. A deep, ominous voice announces that the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed, and a new skill appears: the Daughter's Kiss. Carl spends it on a single fleeing duende, with a stomp. The creature vanishes without resistance, the sidewalk shatters, and the shockwave knocks every other duende flat and breaks a window. There is nothing left to loot. The glow on the patch goes out, and the bar grows each time it is drained.
beats.gist: Ten duende kills fill a sewage-colored essence bar, granting Carl the Daughter's Kiss skill.

beats.headline: One species at a time
beats.text: Three more fills and drains on the walk north, and Carl learns how to feed it. When every soul in the patch is the same species, the Daughter's Kiss hits almost twice as hard, and it carries their trick with it: a charge made of nothing but Howling Gulls releases a scream many times stronger than their own. A dog-sized iguana called a Yuanat, hit with a charged punch, turns to dust and leaves a crater ten feet across.
beats.gist: Carl feeds the patch, which hits twice as hard when filled with one species.

beats.headline: Nearly full
beats.text: Six tokens in, the soul bar for Carl's back patch is almost full, and he has a persistent itch at his neck he suspects is the bar's doing. He has felt no obvious ill effect from the patch, only unease each time the bar nears the top. One or two more kills would let him disperse the power. He holds it instead: spent now, the bar would not refill in time for whatever guards the key, not with only deckmasters to kill on the way.
beats.gist: Carl has six tokens in his back patch soul bar and an itch at his neck.

beats.headline: A hole in the world
beats.text: The Ralphie card has dispelled every spell and muted every minion, and Carl counts as a minion. Then the patch fills: The Scavenger's Daughter has been fed. He cannot cast, but this is a skill, and it lets him. He jumps, aims a foot at Tom, and the turkey looks up and asks, 'Gobble?' The kick feels like a hole in the world. Tom is obliterated with everything around him, the north wall bows out, and the ground tilts toward the cliff. The whole barn begins to slide.
beats.gist: The Ralphie card mutes Carl and minions, but the patch lets Carl kick Tom into oblivion.

beats.headline: She opens her eyes
beats.text: A Demon Prince of Sheol arrives in Cuba, and Carl is close enough to count as being in his presence. The Scavenger's Daughter answers: she opens her eyes and fills with dark power. For as long as the effect lasts, every fire spell Carl casts burns with Sheol Fire instead of the ordinary kind. A quest update comes soon after, asking him to question the prince about who killed Geyrun.
beats.gist: A Demon Prince of Sheol arrives in Cuba, causing the Scavenger's Daughter to open her eyes.

beats.headline: Her eyes stay open
beats.text: A goddess enters the realm, and the patch on Carl's jacket responds: the Scavenger's Daughter's eyes remain open, and she fills with even more power. The same notification brings Ysalte's own contribution, a temporary effect that turns any potion quaffed or handled outside an inventory into vinegar. It also promises the potions will come back as more powerful versions of themselves once she is banished.
beats.gist: A goddess enters the realm, the Scavenger's Daughter's eyes stay open, and Ysalte turns potions into vinegar.

beats.headline: Power left to linger
beats.text: Since the fight in the building, the bar in Carl's interface has crackled with black energy: the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed, and wants her wrath unleashed. He does not unleash it. At the last moment Princess Donut sees the jacket glowing, and says the patch is not an aardvark but a giant centipede crawling through the skulls. A voice in Carl's mind says he should never have let the soul power linger. It needs him alive, and reasonably sane. He had forgotten to activate the Daughter's Kiss.
beats.gist: Black energy crackles in Carl's interface because he did not activate the Daughter's Kiss.

beats.headline: Soul poisoning, and a dead shark
beats.text: The soul energy Carl never spent at the end of the last floor is still riding in the back patch, and it comes due on arrival as Soul Poisoning: jolts of pain, partly blocked by his Emberus ring, with worse effects promised. Saferoom rules cover the city for sixty hours, so nothing alive can be hurt. He finds something dead instead, tosses a suffocated concierge shark into the air and punches it with Daughter's Kiss. The shark vaporises, Carl and Donut are blown back through the mud, and the AI makes up an achievement on the spot: Sushi Smoothie.
beats.gist: Carl punches a suffocated concierge shark with Daughter's Kiss, triggering the Sushi Smoothie achievement.

beats.headline: Fed on the barracks roof
beats.text: An invisible Dreadnaught in a Viceroy mask, J IronFjord, comes at Carl's back on the barracks roof with a glowing dagger. Carl punches him in the chest, rips off the mask, and goes on punching until the man has no face left. A summoned 1970's Death Cult Leader watches and calls it really nasty. The Scavenger's Daughter has been fed. Unleash her wrath. At the end of the fight, when the last worm-ridden mage runs uphill, Carl activates Daughter's Kiss and jumps off the second story onto him.
beats.gist: Carl punches J IronFjord in the chest and face to feed the Scavenger's Daughter.

beats.headline: The War Mages leave with it
beats.text: Akuma tells the Warlord Chat they have found it and are quitting the floor. He uses the same breath to warn Carl and Donut about Agatha.
beats.gist: Akuma tells the Warlord Chat they found the upgrade patch and warns Carl and Donut about Agatha.

beats.headline: Fed, and spent on a skull
beats.text: Mid-race the notification lands: the Scavenger's Daughter has been fed; unleash her wrath. The complication is timing. Carl has to spend it before the finish line or carry it until the next race. So it goes into the kaiju skull at the bottom of the hill: Daughter's Kiss, delivered through a pair of dead kangaroo feet by a man lying on his back on the hood of a food truck. The skull explodes.
beats.gist: Carl feeds the Scavenger's Daughter and spends the upgrade on a kaiju skull.

beats.headline: She opens her eyes for Eris
beats.text: Eris enters the realm and the Scavenger's Daughter opens her eyes and fills with power. The goddess of chaos brings a different effect every time; this one takes a random temporary magic from someone near Carl, not Carl, and makes it permanent. Eris points at Imani and says she will be able to explain it once the goddess has gone.
beats.gist: Eris enters the realm, the Scavenger's Daughter opens her eyes, and Imani gets a permanent random magic.

beats.headline: One aura inside, one outside
beats.text: Inside the boss, the patch does what Rosetta and Mordecai said it would. Beside Taranis: lightning attacks half again as strong, lightning damage taken doubled. In the club, near Emberus instead: immunity to Sheol-based attacks. Khepri, when he is summoned, is too distant to register. The kneepads Penny is wearing give her the same temporary deity effects, and that matters more than anything else they do.
beats.gist: The patch grants lightning attacks and damage effects near Taranis and Sheol immunity near Emberus.

beats.headline: Every inventory changes hands at once
beats.text: Eris fires the effect and each crawler's inventory swaps with whoever is nearest. Donut receives Carl's, and he immediately asks her to combine a bomb and an enriched pet biscuit.
beats.gist: Eris fires an upgrade patch and swaps every crawler's inventory with the nearest person.

recap.text: Carl opens a celestial predator box and gets a divine back patch. He feeds it with duende kills to unlock the Daughter's Kiss, a stomp that shatters sidewalks. He turns a dog-sized iguana to dust and kicks a turkey named Tom with a force like a hole in the world. The patch fills with power near a Demon Prince of Sheol and a goddess, but Carl forgets to activate the Daughter's Kiss.

Soul energy from the previous floor causes Carl Soul Poisoning, which his Emberus ring partly blocks. Carl punches a suffocated concierge shark with Daughter's Kiss, vaporizing the shark and earning the Sushi Smoothie achievement. On a barracks roof, Carl punches J IronFjord until the man has no face. Carl activates Daughter's Kiss and jumps off a second story onto a worm-ridden mage. Akuma tells the Warlord Chat the War Mages found it and warns Carl and Donut about Agatha.

Carl spends the Scavenger's Daughter through a pair of dead kangaroo feet into a kaiju skull, which explodes. Eris makes a random temporary magic permanent for Imani. The upgrade patch doubles lightning damage taken near Taranis but provides immunity to Sheol-based attacks near Emberus. Eris swaps every crawler's inventory with the nearest person, and Donut asks Carl to combine a bomb and an enriched pet biscuit.

tagline.text: Nothing! is a double-width space on the Desperado Club's wheel of fortune. At the roulette table, a player who lands on its twin falls through the floor, and a ghostly clawed arm rises out of the dark after him.
The Nothing is where gods are banished, as Samantha's own father banished her. Her first escape split her in two, and every time a Gate portal closes, one of those inside gets through.

beats.headline: What escaping it costs
beats.text: Psamathe tried to get out and ended up as half a soul in a doll's head. Every closing Gate portal lets one of the inmates through on the opening side. The winding box alone is a direct conduit — wound and fed a stream of charged energy it will drop an entire location, up to a whole necropolis, into the void.
beats.gist: Psamathe became half a soul in a doll's head trying to escape the Nothing.

beats.headline: Psamathe, we are coming
beats.text: When Signet falls, the floor rends open and the Nothing shows itself: ethereal shrieks, black wisps and tendrils lashing upward, a stench of sulphur. And from the dark a faint voice, distant and hollow, shrieking a name. Psamathe. Psamathe, we are coming. Then the hole snaps shut. Apito has turned her back, the notice says. The seal has been broken, the Butcher's Masquerade has failed to cast, and the party is over.
beats.gist: The Nothing shows itself with black wisps and a sulphur stench before the hole snaps shut.

beats.headline: A thousand names, and a life's work
beats.text: The room wants to know what Juice Box just turned into, and Architect Houston of the Viceroys answers: the personification of the Nothing is one way to describe it. Then, raising his voice for once: a creature with no single name, which some people see at the moment of death; perhaps not a deity at all but a trans-dimensional entity, like the Apothecary. The Hag. The Unwashed. The Stalker. The Last Light. The Thirst. The Viceroys call it the Beautiful Place. Cascadia says it is banned as a mob. After a moment he adds, somewhat wistfully, that gaining access to it is his life's work.
beats.gist: Architect Houston describes the personification of the Nothing as a trans-dimensional entity and his life's work.

beats.headline: Broken
beats.text: The crawlers arrive on the tenth floor to find Justice Light dead and the Nothing broken.
beats.gist: Crawlers arrive on the tenth floor and find Justice Light dead and the Nothing broken.

beats.headline: Tem, as scenery
beats.text: The thing blocking the road before the finish line is the skull of Tem, a beetle whose skull alone stands three storeys tall, who resided within the Nothing until a few days ago. Odette wasted him the moment he appeared, and the AI, waste not, want not, has been borrowing parts of the corpse for different races because he was really badass-looking. It suggests the crawlers take note of his size. He has friends who are still alive.
beats.gist: The skull of Tem blocks the road, standing three storeys tall.

beats.headline: Nothing, in quotation marks
beats.text: The plan was always the casino. Akuma insisted that a broken Nothing still leaves its spot on the Wheel of Fortune, and that the portal would drop anyone who used it into a catchall holding area, where Herot, inside the Pineapple Cabaret, could pull them out. Safer than a cleaner bot, and more at once. Then Pontiff reports from inside the club: the wheel does show Nothing again, but now it wears quotation marks. Nobody likes quotation marks.
beats.gist: Akuma plans for the portal to drop people into a catchall area for Herot to retrieve.

beats.headline: A portal to a stasis chamber
beats.text: Mitch the croupier sets the Wheel of Fortune by hand to the last click of the first Nothing wedge and hits a button, and a black portal opens under the stand-here spot. Crawler Carl remembers the real Nothing's heavy mental pull. This one has none; it is as inert as a door. His failing implant reads it as an Enhancement Zone Subspace Portal, one-way, open access, leading to a stasis chamber. It stays open about fifteen seconds. Chris drops through. It is exactly what they hoped it would say.
beats.gist: Mitch the croupier opens a black portal to a stasis chamber for Chris to drop through.

recap.text: Psamathe tried to escape the prison dimension and became half a soul in a doll's head. One inmate passes through the opening side of every closing Gate portal. A winding box fed a stream of charged energy drops a location, up to a whole necropolis, into the void.

Signet falls and the floor rends open to show the Nothing, which has ethereal shrieks, black wisps, lashing tendrils, and a stench of sulphur. A hollow voice shrieks that they are coming for Psamathe before the hole snaps shut. The Butcher's Masquerade failed to cast and the seal is broken because Apito turned her back.

Architect Houston of the Viceroys tells a room that Juice Box became the personification of the Nothing. He describes it as a trans-dimensional entity like the Apothecary, known as The Hag, The Unwashed, The Stalker, The Last Light, The Thirst, or the Beautiful Place. Cascadia bans it as a mob, but Houston says accessing it is his life's work.

Crawlers find Justice Light dead and the Nothing broken. They pass the three-storey tall skull of Tem, a beetle the AI borrowed for races. Akuma and Herot use the broken Nothing as a portal to the Pineapple Cabaret. Mitch the croupier sets the Wheel of Fortune, and Chris drops through a one-way portal to a stasis chamber.

tagline.text: The fans voted Carl a xistera: a scoop that looks like wicker, strapped to his forearm and reaching two and a half feet past his hand, which hurls whatever he pulls from his inventory into it.

An emergency box has sent Carl an extension slot for his xistera, built for one purpose: throwing Samantha's head, five hundred metres for every point of his strength. Take the slot off, and she comes back to him.

description.text: Enchanted Xistera Extension Slot (Head-throwing attachment). This is a unique item! This item was created especially for Crawler Carl by The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, Intergalactic NFC. Attaches to the end of a xistera. Allows for the tossing of a head. This special edition head tosser is custom made to fit decapitated love doll heads. When tossing a head of a withering spirit, the distance traveled will be greatly enhanced. (500 meters x Strength) Tossed head will be magically returned once the extension slot is removed from xistera.

beats.headline: Voted in by an audience
beats.text: The first fan boxes come open in the Over City. Donut draws a framed photograph of Bea and Brad. Carl draws a xistera: a wicker-looking scoop reaching two and a half feet past his hand that straps to his hand and arm and hurls whatever he pulls out of his inventory into it, adjusting itself around the shape of the thing. It makes his slingshot redundant.
beats.gist: Carl draws a xistera, a wicker-looking scoop that hurls inventory items, making his slingshot redundant.

beats.headline: Banger Spheres
beats.text: The close fighting on the trains has kept it mostly idle this floor. On the platform at 283, Carl loads a Banger Sphere, one of a few hundred baseball-sized balls of dwarven robot scrap he made at the engineering table; the system names only that size. The first catches a babababoon in the neck when he was aiming between the eyes. It dies anyway. He throws two more at the two mobs on the other side of the platform, and they die too.
beats.gist: Carl throws baseball-sized Banger Spheres of dwarven robot scrap to kill a babababoon and two mobs.

beats.headline: The extension slot
beats.text: An emergency box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network holds an attachment built for exactly one crawler and exactly one purpose. Screwed onto the end of the scoop it lets him throw Samantha, and it multiplies his reach: five hundred metres for every point of strength. Take the slot off and she comes back to him.
beats.gist: An emergency box holds an attachment that lets a crawler throw Samantha five hundred metres per strength point.

beats.headline: Ren's exit
beats.text: The plan runs on teleport traps, two keys, and Samantha arriving somewhere she cannot walk to. Quan Ch surfaces at Ren's exit. Carl throws her over downtown to the capitol with the scoop, then teleports in behind her.
beats.gist: Carl throws Quan Ch with the scoop to the capitol and teleports in behind her.

beats.headline: A bomb, a biscuit and an open mouth
beats.text: Every crawler's inventory swaps hands at once and Donut is holding Carl's. He talks her through combining a bomb with an enriched pet biscuit, takes the result off her, and puts it down Scolopendra's throat with the scoop. She comes apart into a puddle.
beats.gist: Inventories swap and Carl uses a scoop to put a bomb and enriched pet biscuit down Scolopendra's throat.

recap.text: Fan boxes open in the Over City. Donut draws a framed photograph of Bea and Brad. Carl draws a xistera, a wicker-looking scoop reaching two and a half feet past his hand that straps to his arm and hurls inventory items, making his slingshot redundant.
