Carl loads a Banger Sphere, a baseball-sized ball of dwarven robot scrap made at the engineering table. He hits a babababoon in the neck instead of between the eyes, and it dies. He throws two more spheres at two mobs on the platform at 283, and they die too.

An emergency box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network holds an attachment for one crawler and one purpose. Screwed onto the end of the scoop, it lets Carl throw Samantha five hundred metres for every point of strength. Removing the slot brings her back to him.

The plan uses teleport traps, two keys, and Samantha arriving where she cannot walk. Quan Ch surfaces at Ren's exit. Carl throws her over downtown to the capitol with the scoop and teleports in behind her.

Every crawler's inventory swaps hands and Donut holds Carl's. Donut tells Xistera to combine a bomb with an enriched pet biscuit. Donut takes the result and puts it down Scolopendra's throat with the scoop, and she comes apart into a puddle.

tagline.text: A Skill Potion from a gold box raises one named skill by a single level.

Not every skill potion is worth a single level. On his show, the Maestro gave Frank and Maggie a legendary one that takes Find Crawler to level fifteen, and there is exactly one crawler Maggie wants found.

description.text: Skill Potion. Drinking this adds a single level to the Determine Value skill. Hopefully now you'll realize all those Magic: The Gathering cards are nothing more than just meaningless pieces of paper, and you should have spent your money on something with actual value, like a treadmill. Or shampoo.

beats.headline: Find Crawler
beats.text: Carl's trap closes on Yvette, and her own mother finishes what the trap started. On his show, the Maestro hands Frank and Maggie My a Legendary Skill Potion that takes Find Crawler to level 15, and Maggie snatches it up. There is exactly one crawler she wants found.
beats.gist: Carl traps Yvette and her mother finishes her; Maggie snatches a level 15 Find Crawler potion.

beats.headline: Acute Ears, in a safe room
beats.text: Donut drinks one and comes up with Acute Ears, plus fang caps for Mongo. Carl comes out of the same haul with a great deal of explosive and a Scroll of Upgrade that improves his boxers, which is roughly the ratio he has come to expect.
beats.gist: Donut drinks a Skill Potion for Acute Ears and gets fang caps for Mongo.

beats.headline: Hell-Kissed, Celestial, and the Prince of Woe
beats.text: A gold pet box, a patch that opens the Midnight Market, and the Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe. The potion hands Carl the Gloom Wraith Phase, which is a skill for walking through people.
beats.gist: Carl drinks the Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe to walk through people.

beats.headline: Platinum Hotlist Expansion
beats.text: The Platinum Boss Box for Prison Pocket holds an upgrade potion: Platinum Hotlist Expansion. Carl sends the description to Mordecai and drinks it over the aftertaste of liquefied fish from his broken food box. Twenty hotlist spaces become twenty-five, and a new tab opens for the Contingency skill: up to ten programmable automations, each able to fire several hotlist items at once under conditions he sets. Lucia Mar, he suspects, already has this.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a Platinum Hotlist Expansion potion over the aftertaste of liquefied fish.

recap.text: Carl's trap closes on Yvette, and her mother finishes what the trap started. The Maestro hands Frank and Maggie My a Legendary Skill Potion that takes Find Crawler to level 15. Maggie snatches the potion to find one specific crawler.
Donut drinks a potion in a safe room and gets Acute Ears and fang caps for Mongo. Carl gets explosive and a Scroll of Upgrade for his boxers.

Carl receives a gold pet box, a patch that opens the Midnight Market, and the Hell-Kissed Celestial Skill Potion of the Prince of Woe. The potion gives Carl the Gloom Wraith Phase skill for walking through people.

Carl finds a Platinum Hotlist Expansion potion in the Platinum Boss Box for Prison Pocket. He drinks it over the aftertaste of liquefied fish from a broken food box. His hotlist spaces increase from twenty to twenty-five, and he opens a Contingency skill tab for ten programmable automations. Carl suspects Lucia Mar already has this.

entities.name: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo

tagline.text: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo came out of a Gold Prepotente Box, and Carl cannot trade it, destroy it or throw it away. It is named after the message boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.
The System has dropped Carl a heavy hint, in the name of a box, that the Voodoo book can be used together with his ability tattoo, and then declined to say how.

description.text: When you meet a crawler who owns this same item, their name will permanently appear in this enchanted book. You may use the book to exchange messages. You may write your message under their name, and only they will receive it. If you write under your own name, everyone who has your entry will see the message. You may write your message manually or using the messaging interface while turned to the page. One must open the book to read the message, but you will have the option to copy the words. Message will erase on demand, allowing one to write a new note. This book is not retroactively filled with the entries of people you have already met. You must be within close-ish vicinity of them for their name to be added. Works only with crawlers who also own this book.

beats.headline: Out of a Gold Prepotente Box
beats.text: Donut has just told Carl she is frightened and does not want to be in charge. Carl opens a Gold Prepotente Box and finds a book he cannot trade, cannot destroy and cannot throw away. Drop it and it is back in his inventory. It is named for the pin boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.
beats.gist: Carl opens a Gold Prepotente Box and finds The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo.

beats.headline: The AI drops a hint
beats.text: Going through his boxes, Carl collects an achievement for using a borrowed skill through the ability tattoo. The System volunteers, unprompted, that there is a way to put the two together with the book, and then declines to say what it is.
beats.gist: Carl collects an achievement; the System hints at a connection with the Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo.

beats.headline: A map from Burcu, slammed shut
beats.text: Inside the Madness castle Carl finds the crawler Burcu held beside Architect Houston, and his message to her is refused and logged for the adjutant: planning with a non-member. Then his Book of Voodoo updates with an entry from her. She is drawing a map of the surgical theatre, a line of Xs marked Fireball traps, and starting to write something about Houston, when it slams shut on its own. The accompanying warning: this is still cheating, you clown. Nice try. It is meant for something else.
beats.gist: The Book of Voodoo shows Burcu's map of Fireball traps, then slams shut with a warning.

beats.headline: Carl's Book of Boom
beats.text: Updated with, in the System's words, a metric fuckton of entries, and split into two volumes; the second is Carl's Book of Boom. It should run to almost thirty thousand pages and holds about five hundred, opening near the entry it wants read. Crawler 1,982,122, Asi Hamami, a level 59 fox warrior, has left a note of thanks and a crude red lock and key: eat the page for a level 10 Lockpick skill for five minutes. The crawlers who painted these lose the skills for good. Donut gets a book of her own, A Banquet Fit for a Princess.
beats.gist: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo splits into two volumes, including Carl's Book of Boom.

beats.headline: A spell each, on the way out
beats.text: Of 989 crawlers left, 715 are stepping into the Outreach Guild and not coming back out. On their way they strip their vehicles, trade their upgrades, and, every one of them, use Milk's method to write a spell into the Voodoo Book before they go. The crawlers staying get a thinner field and a thicker book. It is the last thing most of them do in the dungeon, and it is done for somebody else.
beats.gist: Crawlers write spells into the Voodoo Book for others before entering the Outreach Guild.

recap.text: Donut tells Carl she is frightened and does not want to be in charge. Carl opens a Gold Prepotente Box and finds The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo. He cannot trade, destroy, or throw away the book, and it returns to his inventory if dropped. The System names it after pin boards at old conventions.

Carl collects an achievement for using a borrowed skill through an ability tattoo, and the System hints the Book of Voodoo can combine them. The book updates with Burcu's map of the surgical theatre and Fireball traps before slamming shut. It splits into two volumes, including Carl's Book of Boom, and contains a note from Asi Hamami to eat a page for a level 10 Lockpick skill. Donut gets A Banquet Fit for a Princess.

Of 989 crawlers, 715 enter the Outreach Guild and do not return. Before they go, they strip their vehicles and trade upgrades. Each crawler uses Milk's method to write a spell into the Voodoo Book for someone else.

tagline.text: A Fan Box holds items voted for by the crawler's followers. Once you receive one, you cannot open it for thirty hours while the fans vote.
A Fan Box is the prize for being watched: the audience votes on what goes inside, and the crawler carries it around for thirty hours, knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.

beats.headline: The prize for being watched
beats.text: Awarded for gathering a following, or for doing something in front of enough people that the following gathers itself. The contents are put to an audience vote, and the box will not open for thirty hours, so the crawler carries it around knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.
beats.gist: A Fan Box is awarded for gathering a following, and an audience votes on its contents.

beats.headline: The holdings of the defeated
beats.text: The legendary fan box rises as a cobra head to the ceiling of the safe room, earned because a large share of the Naga system was watching Carl just before he executed Rishi. By a Naga jury's vote it is his wedding gift: the holdings of the defeated. What comes out is garbage. Wet, scorched clothes, wrecked furniture, a shot-through microwave, a melted trophy for eighth place at GreaserBall with the place removed from the plaque. It keeps coming until the pile nearly reaches the ceiling and blocks the bathroom. The box allows that there might be a useful thing or two in there.
beats.gist: A legendary fan box gives Carl the holdings of the defeated, which are mostly garbage.

recap.text: A crawler receives a Fan Box for gathering a following or doing something in front of enough people. An audience votes on the contents. The box remains closed for thirty hours while strangers argue about what the crawler deserves.

A legendary fan box rises as a cobra head to the ceiling of a safe room. It gives Carl the holdings of the defeated because the Naga system watched him execute Rishi. The box spews wet clothes, a shot-through microwave, and a melted eighth place GreaserBall trophy until the pile blocks the bathroom.

tagline.text: Only a patron can send a Benefactor Box, and they hold the rarest items. According to Mordecai, even a bronze Benefactor Box is better than a plain gold Adventurer Box.
A Benefactor Box is bought for you by somebody out there who wants you to keep going, and it may hold things from the patron's home world that the dungeon itself would never give you.

beats.headline: Three patron spots, at auction
beats.text: Patronage changes this season. Every crawler is limited to three patrons, the spots auctioned for one day each at the start of the fourth, fifth and sixth floors, opening at one credit, so virtually every living crawler will have one. What a patron bids above the standard fee comes back as discounts on the boxes they send; bid below it and their boxes cost more. The more a patron pays, the more and better the Benefactor Boxes, and the higher a crawler's social numbers, the better the loot. Patrons may transfer from the seventh floor.
beats.gist: Patronage limits crawlers to three spots auctioned for one credit at the fourth, fifth, and sixth floors.

beats.headline: Bronze from a sponsor beats gold from the floor
beats.text: Only a sponsor can send one. They use the same six quality tiers as every other box and they outclass the ordinary run of loot at every rank, so a bronze one from a benefactor is worth more than a gold one earned. It means the fastest way to be well equipped is to be liked by someone with money.
beats.gist: A benefactor sends a sponsor box that outclasses ordinary loot, making bronze worth more than gold.

recap.text: Patronage changes this season. Every crawler has three patron spots auctioned for one day at the start of the fourth, fifth and sixth floors. Bids above the standard fee create discounts on boxes, while bids below make boxes cost more. Higher payments and social numbers result in better loot in Benefactor Boxes. Patrons may transfer from the seventh floor.
Sponsors send boxes using six quality tiers. A bronze box from a benefactor outclasses gold loot earned on the floor. Being liked by someone with money is the fastest way to be well equipped.

entities.name: The Royal Chariot
entities.tagline: The Royal Chariot is a tracked contraption that Carl and Katia built by hand around a magical train-cart engine. Donut named it before it was finished, and the System's description of it is mostly abuse.
entities.description: Tracked All-Terrain Suicide Machine. The Royal Chariot – Contraption. If a snowmobile got drunk on moonshine and had a sweaty, ill-advised night with a hillbilly’s coon-hunting ATV, this oversized birth defect of a vehicle would be the result.

beats.headline: Built on the floor it is meant to cross
beats.text: Carl and Katia build it at the engineering and metalworking tables around a single-gear magical train cart engine, and trade metal tires for a wide snowmobile track once the metal bogs down in the sand. Donut names it before it is finished. The System's description reads as abuse, and Katia collects an achievement for inventing it.
beats.gist: Carl and Katia build the Royal Chariot around a single-gear magical train cart engine.

recap.text: Carl and Katia build the Royal Chariot at engineering and metalworking tables around a single-gear magical train cart engine. They trade metal tires for a wide snowmobile track when the metal bogs down in the sand. Donut names it before it is finished, and Katia collects an achievement for inventing it.

entities.name: Cleaner Bot
entities.tagline: A Cleaner Bot is one of the cheapest personal-space upgrades, at twenty-five thousand gold. Katia bought one without a word, because the room was swimming in ghoul blood.

beats.headline: Bought for the housekeeping
beats.text: A personal space upgrade bought from the Bopca for twenty-five thousand gold, one of the cheapest there is. Katia pays without a word, because the room is swimming in ghoul blood, and the bot sets to work at once. It is going to take a long time.
beats.gist: Katia pays twenty-five thousand gold for a personal space upgrade to clean ghoul blood.

beats.headline: A white one, pocketed
beats.text: In the surgical theatre of the Madness castle, the fourth table is empty and drenched in blood, and a cleaner bot of the same model as the crew's own, painted solid white, is slurping it off the floor. Carl lands on that table, slips in the blood and goes flat on his back. The bot shrieks, beeps and comes at him. He apologises, grabs it in both hands, feels the buzz that means it will go in his inventory, and puts it there, somewhat to his own surprise.
beats.gist: Carl slips in blood on an empty table in the Madness castle and pockets a white bot.

beats.headline: A second bot, reset
beats.text: The cleaner bot has a disintegration ray. It uses it on the broken kitchen table, beeping with satisfaction at each puff of smoke, and then it faces a mountain of a dead naga's junk and very nearly has a heart attack. Carl hands Mordecai the second cleaner bot, a slightly smaller white one, an old model with blood on it from Architect Houston's operating theater, and asks him to get it working for them before anything valuable gets zapped. Mordecai switches it off to reset it. The two bots beep at each other.
beats.gist: The cleaner bot zaps a table, then faces a naga's junk; Carl gives Mordecai another bot.

beats.headline: Sold out due to overwhelming demand
beats.text: Since the previous floor, crawlers have been complaining that the Cleaner Bot upgrade is missing from the personal space shop, due to "overwhelming demand." Everyone blamed warlords stockpiling for Faction Wars, which was partly true. The white one Carl looted from Architect Houston's surgical theatre was an old model and, as it happens, the last one the store had. The rest of the demand has a single name: Herot, with a standing order to buy every cleaner bot that shows up. Which makes a household appliance the most interesting item in the shop.
beats.gist: Crawlers blame warlords for the missing Cleaner Bot upgrade, but Herot buys every unit.

beats.headline: Suckira, and Ezra Fitz the Second
beats.text: There are two cleaner bots now, so Donut insists on names. The white one is Suckira, after the robot vacuum Louis's mother had in Florida; Louis won the right in a coin flip that Samantha conducted and says she rigged. The other is Ezra Fitz the Second, because, Donut explains, Ezra Fitz sucks. The method is a sale: crawler into an XL pet carrier, carrier into the bot's weight-based storage, bot into the shop, where Herot buys it. One bot holds perhaps fifty people, and a sold bot cannot be relisted for thirty days.
beats.gist: Donut names the white bot Suckira and the other Ezra Fitz the Second.

beats.headline: Forty seats, and a hundred and five
beats.text: The Pineapple Cabaret transfer goes smoothly. Carl's cleaner bot fits forty people. The one belonging to Bobby Montague, the Illusionist with the tall hair, somehow fits a hundred and five. Two hundred and twenty-seven crawlers go across, not counting Li Na, among them Zhang, Tran, Bautista and Archie. All the cleaner bots were bought up immediately, which is a strange career for a housekeeping upgrade.
beats.gist: Carl's cleaner bot fits forty people, but Bobby Montague's fits a hundred and five.

recap.text: Katia pays twenty-five thousand gold to the Bopca for a personal space upgrade for the bot. The room swims in ghoul blood, and the bot sets to work. It is going to take a long time.

Carl finds a white cleaner bot slurping blood off an empty table in the surgical theatre of the Madness castle. Carl slips in the blood and falls on his back. The bot shrieks and beeps, so Carl grabs it in both hands and puts it in his inventory.

A cleaner bot uses a disintegration ray on a kitchen table and a dead naga's junk. Carl gives Mordecai a smaller white bot from Architect Houston's operating theater to reset. Donut names the bots Suckira and Ezra Fitz the Second. Herot buys every cleaner bot in the shop, and Carl uses one to move forty people, including Zhang, Tran, Bautista, and Archie, to the Pineapple Cabaret.

entities.name: Party Planner
entities.tagline: Party Planner is a silver tilt-rotor airship that came out of the celestial box Louis earned by outliving a goddess's mark for death. He gave it the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.
entities.description: Casket in the Sky. Party Planner. Tilt Rotor Stealth Light Bomber. Vehicle. This vehicle is classed as tier three Armor.

beats.headline: The reward for having survived being condemned
beats.text: It comes out of the celestial box Louis earned for outliving a goddess's mark for death on the floor before. Two items: a tier III guild upgrade called an Airship Portal, and the ship itself, a silver tilt-rotor he names Party Planner, the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.
beats.gist: Louis takes an Airship Portal and a silver tilt-rotor named Party Planner from a celestial box.

beats.headline: Ripped down the middle
beats.text: Party Planner, the airship, has been destroyed. On its next sortie, the gravity-magic dragon circling the Reaver castle came straight at it, and General Louis hit it with missiles, which only made it angry. It cast a spell and ripped the ship in half down the middle. The bombs dropped out before they were armed and did not go off. The two replacement door gunners, borrowed from a clinic, are believed dead. Louis went out by feather fall, dropping straight toward the Reaver castle, which he means to hit by himself.
beats.gist: A gravity-magic dragon rips the airship Party Planner in half, killing two clinic door gunners.

recap.text: Louis uses a celestial box to get an Airship Portal and a silver tilt-rotor he names Party Planner. A gravity-magic dragon circling the Reaver castle casts a spell and rips Party Planner in half down the middle. Bombs drop without arming, and two door gunners from a clinic are believed dead. Louis uses feather fall to drop toward the Reaver castle.

entities.name: Goblin Copper Chopper
entities.tagline: The Goblin Copper Chopper is a steam-driven goblin motorcycle with a sidecar: a single wheel on a huge spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, which Donut began demanding changes to the moment she sat in it.
entities.description: Goblin Copper Chopper with attached sidecar. Human-sized. Contraption. Take a junkyard bicycle, add an unreliable steam engine, remove all the bolts holding it together.

beats.headline: Steam, two wheels and a seat for royalty
beats.text: Goblin-made, steam-driven, and assembled with an optimism the materials do not support. The sidecar is a bar, a single wheel on a colossal spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, and Donut starts demanding changes to it the moment she has sat in it.
beats.gist: The Goblin Copper Chopper is a steam-driven contraption with a fur-lined orc skull seat.

beats.headline: Three miles to a lump of coal
beats.text: Its first real run: east out of Seattle for hours, three or four miles to a lump of coal and perhaps twenty miles an hour. It has pedals and a throttle; the rider pumps up to speed and the throttle locks it there. The engine in the chassis runs hot enough that a man without pants rides with his legs held out. At Chopper Pilot five the throttle will go faster. The faster it goes, the tighter the fog of war closes in, and mobs twenty feet off the artery do not show until it stops.
beats.gist: The Goblin Copper Chopper travels twenty miles an hour and requires the rider to pump pedals.

beats.headline: Into the stairwell
beats.text: Boiler breach imminent: fifteen seconds. The pilot cannot remember which valve releases the pressure, so he opens the throttle instead. The Goblin Copper Chopper hauls the Mother of All Bombs into the stairwell chamber, its trailer spraying oil across the floor, and goes over the edge of the hole without its riders, who jump. A crunch. A relatively small explosion. Black smoke billows out of the stairwell.
beats.gist: The Goblin Copper Chopper hauls the Mother of All Bombs into the stairwell and explodes.

recap.text: The Goblin Copper Chopper is a steam-driven contraption with a fur-lined orc skull for a seat and a bar for a sidecar. It travels twenty miles an hour, forcing a man without pants to hold his legs out because the engine runs hot. The vehicle hauls the Mother of All Bombs into a stairwell chamber, sprays oil, and falls into a hole. It produces a crunch, a small explosion, and black smoke.

entities.name: Carl's Jug O' Boom

tagline.text: Carl's Jug O' Boom is a clay jug of Rev-Up moonshine with a splash of goblin oil and a short torch jammed in like a cork. It throws blue flames up to the ceiling, and the dungeon has named it after him.
The Jug O' Boom is now in the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name, and he earns a gold coin for every kill another crawler makes with it, for the rest of his life.
The moonshine the Jug O' Boom needs is no longer being made, and Carl's royalties stopped after the first few coins.

entities.description: Created by an unstable, pantsless man who talks to a cat, Carl's Jug O' Boom takes the bigger-is-better approach when it comes to hobgoblin fire bottles. Burns hotter, bigger, and faster than your normal Molotov Cocktail. The use of a standard torch instead of a cloth wick makes these devices much more stable. Just don't drop it once it's lit, lest you find yourself doing a Joan of Arc impersonation.

beats.headline: They named it after him
beats.text: Twenty-five clay jugs of Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine, looted off clurichauns. Pour a splash out, add a couple of ounces of goblin oil, and jam a short torch into the mouth, where it fits like a cork. The test throw: an insignificant explosion, then blue flames splashing like water across the room, high enough to reach the ceiling. The dungeon names the result Carl's Jug O' Boom. "Carl, look, they named it after you!" He sees.
beats.gist: Carl creates an incendiary tossable from clurichaun moonshine, goblin oil, and a short torch.

beats.headline: Two for the laminak
beats.text: The moonshine is made nearby, where dozens of clurichauns fill jugs from a filthy aluminium bathtub under two fairy managers. Crawler Donut lures the fairies out; Crawler Carl lights two jugs and tosses them in among the forty workers. Afterwards he collects everything that survived: eighty empty jugs and sixty full ones. He leaves the moonshine in the tub alone, in case touching it blinds him.
beats.gist: Carl tosses two lit jugs of moonshine at forty clurichauns and collects eighty empty and sixty full jugs.

beats.headline: Carried in by a zombie
beats.text: The delivery method for the Krakaren's chamber is a zombified clurichaun. On Crawler Donut's order it holds a jug over its head, like the boombox in Say Anything, a stick of dynamite shoved down its overalls for good measure; the torch is lit, and it runs through the doorway. Crawler Carl dives behind a shield, puts the alchemy table over himself and the cat like a clamshell, and wraps himself around her before the explosion comes.
beats.gist: A zombified clurichaun carries a jug over its head and a stick of dynamite in its overalls.

beats.headline: Dungeonpreneur, and a Codex entry
beats.text: New achievement: Dungeonpreneur, for inventing a stackable weapon, device or potion. The recipe goes into the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name. The reward: one gold coin for every kill made with it by other crawlers, payable for the rest of his natural life if he survives, even in future seasons. The lawyers insisted on that last part. The citation adds that he is going to die, and the dungeon is going to keep using his work.
beats.gist: Carl invents the Jug O' Boom, a stackable incendiary tossable, and earns the Dungeonpreneur achievement.

beats.headline: Almost a quarter of an elemental
beats.text: From the safe room doorway, Crawler Carl tosses a lit jug at the back of the rage elemental and slams the door. The recap shows the rest: the show pauses on the recipe, stamps Added to the Dungeon Codex over his mugshot, and then the monster's health plummets almost twenty-five percent. It is stunned for a good ten seconds, and the napalm-like fire slows its healing.
beats.gist: Carl tosses a lit Jug O' Boom at a rage elemental, stunning it for ten seconds.

beats.headline: Boom babies down the hall
beats.text: Carts on free-weight wheels, dropped off the back of the trailer into the hallway behind it with the rage elemental in pursuit. Baby Uno carries three boom jugs, a jug of goblin oil, a jar of gunpowder and the last of the hobgoblin pus. There are boom jar babies, shredder babies, and the oh shit babies, which pair two boom jars with a gunpowder satchel wrapped in dynamite. They carpet bomb the hall, and whatever does not light itself, Crawler Donut lights with a low magic missile.
beats.gist: Baby Uno carpet bombs a hallway with boom jugs, goblin oil, gunpowder, and hobgoblin pus.

beats.headline: Four kills, one coin each
beats.text: A new tab in the interface: ACCOUNTS. One item. Creator's Fee, Carl's Jug O' Boom. Royalty: 1 gold coin per kill. Current kills: 4. The small print, too small to zoom: the count updates once daily, and two gold coins plus a 25% deposit fee, rounded up, are deducted upon cash out. Four kills, all by other crawlers' hands.
beats.gist: Carl's Jug O' Boom earns one gold coin per kill via the ACCOUNTS tab.

beats.headline: Frozen in mid-air
beats.text: Crawler Carl lights a jug and throws it at the barn doors of a neighbourhood boss's chamber as they open, just as about forty cheering kobolds come pouring out. The world freezes with the jug hanging in the air like a comet while the dungeon introduces the boss. When it unfreezes, the jug explodes among the kobolds, evaporating most of them, including the boss's owner.
beats.gist: Carl throws a lit Jug O' Boom at barn doors as forty cheering kobolds pour out.

beats.headline: Ten left, and no more moonshine
beats.text: Crawler Carl has ten boom jugs left and a stash of Rev-Up bottles set aside to sell. Quint the pharmacist had heard the Krakaren say no more of the stuff was being made this season; Mordecai says Carl and Donut are the reason it was shut down. The royalties stopped after the first few coins. At least one other crawler found a few bottles.
beats.gist: Carl has ten boom jugs and Rev-Up bottles to sell.

beats.headline: Valued at 7,500 gold
beats.text: Pustule the hobgoblin, asked what a jug is worth, rubs it, whimpers, and licks it. Her verdict: nice design, material cost much too high. A different accelerant would burn less hot and cost ninety percent less, and plain moonshine would sell for more than the bomb. She would sell one for about 7,500 gold and pay half that. Crawler Carl keeps it, for a value reference.
beats.gist: Pustule the hobgoblin values Carl's Jug O' Boom at 7,500 gold.

beats.headline: Mic drop at the temple door
beats.text: A one-armed dwarf child under one arm, a lit jug in the other hand, a swordsman guard swinging. Crawler Carl tosses the jug straight up, Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper takes them all to a rooftop across the street, and the jug comes down on the temple entrance. The remaining eight city elves are crisped instantly. The two guards' health bars barely move.
beats.gist: Carl tosses a lit jug up and Donut's Puddle Jumper moves them to a rooftop.

beats.headline: Twin fireballs at a junction
beats.text: In the station defence, Katia's Crowd Blast carries her into a T-shaped junction packed with krakaren monsters. Crawler Carl follows and throws one jug down each branch as Crawler Donut puddle jumps the three of them back to the main room. Twin fireballs erupt at the far ends. Soon after, the two closest soul crystals pop.
beats.gist: Carl throws a jug down each branch of a T-shaped junction, creating twin fireballs.

beats.headline: Too hot for this job
beats.text: Two jugs left. The sand ooze's core sits under the recliner, and ordinary fire is no good: the ooze has already snuffed out the flames left by Crawler Donut's spell. It needs something that burns hot, and Crawler Carl fears the jugs would burn a little too hot. He uses burn gel instead, a cookbook recipe that Mordecai showed him how to improve. With moonshine and a paste of his, it burns hot and bright with little smoke.
beats.gist: Carl uses moonshine and Mordecai's paste to make burn gel instead of using the Jug O' Boom.

beats.headline: Plain moonshine, nearly the same
beats.text: Against the hydra, Crawler Carl digs through his inventory for jugs. He long ago ran out of his Jug-O-Booms and has only a few regular moonshine jugs left, which are almost the same thing. He lights one and throws it over Alpha Carl's head at the hydra, and it catches one of the replicants in the face.
beats.gist: Carl throws a lit moonshine jug over Alpha Carl's head and hits a replicant in the face.

recap.text: Crawler Carl mixes clurichaun moonshine with goblin oil and a torch to create Carl's Jug O' Boom. The dungeon adds the recipe to the Codex, awarding Carl one gold coin for every kill made by other crawlers. Carl uses the jugs to stun a rage elemental and carpet bomb a hall with babies on free-weight wheels. He throws a jug into a group of forty kobolds, evaporating most of them and the boss's owner.

Carl has ten boom jugs and Rev-Up bottles. Pustule the hobgoblin licks a jug and values it at 7,500 gold. Carl tosses a lit jug into the air and Donut's Puddle Jumper takes them to a rooftop. The jug hits the temple entrance and crisps eight city elves.

Katia's Crowd Blast carries her into a T-shaped junction packed with krakaren monsters. Carl throws one jug down each branch and Donut puddle jumps them back to the main room. Twin fireballs erupt and two soul crystals pop.
Carl has two jugs left. A sand ooze's core sits under a recliner and snuffs out the flames from Donut's spell. Carl uses burn gel made from moonshine and a paste Mordecai helped him improve.

Crawler Carl digs through his inventory for jugs to use against the hydra. He has run out of Jug-O-Booms and uses a regular moonshine jug instead. He lights the jug and throws it over Alpha Carl's head, catching one of the replicants in the face.

tagline.text: The Bolt of Ophiotaurus is a single crossbow bolt from Princess Formidable. It is an ordinary bolt unless it goes straight into a god's eye, and then the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.
The Bolt of Ophiotaurus opened a goddess to a killing blow. Magical bolts can be used again as long as they don't break, and Katia still has this one.
Princess Donut fired Katia's bolt straight into Emberus's eye, and for fifteen seconds the god had no invulnerability. Taranis used them.

description.text: The Bolt of Ophiotaurus. This is 1 of 100. This item acts as a regular crossbow bolt unless it is shot directly into the eye of a deity. Upon a successful strike to the god's eye, the deity's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.

beats.headline: One of a hundred, in a benefactor box
beats.text: Katia's first benefactor box from Princess Formidable holds a single small item, and nobody says anything while she examines it. A crossbow bolt, just the one. It is a regular bolt unless it goes directly into the eye of a deity, in which case the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds. The sender is the youngest sister of the Maestro, now dead, and of Crown Prince Stalwart, who is somewhere in the dungeon. Carl reads the description and decides the sister is not a huge fan of her big brother.
beats.gist: Katia receives a single crossbow bolt from Princess Formidable that pauses a deity's invulnerability for fifteen seconds.

beats.headline: A message, not a plan
beats.text: In the trainyard, Grull, with the Maestro at the controls, told Carl mid-rampage that even the magical bolt his sister wasted on Carl's friend would not work: Carl was not strong enough yet to hurt him. Afterwards, loading the portal cart onto the employee track, Katia wishes she could have used it. Carl says it would have been a waste, since they could not have hurt him, and that the gift was probably more a message to the brother than a plan to kill him. He promises her a use for it.
beats.gist: Grull tells Carl a magical bolt cannot hurt him; Carl tells Katia it was a message.

beats.headline: Into a goddess's eye
beats.text: Ysalte stands in the corpse of Sister Ines, summoned for a boss event and invulnerable on this floor. Donut's all-caps report tells the rest. Katia gave a crawler an arrow thing, and he stuck it into the goddess's eye. Then he blew himself up, the explosion concentrated on her neck, and her head fell off. The system message names him as her slayer, marked for death by every deity except her sworn enemies. He was her own totem.
beats.gist: A crawler sticks an arrow thing into a goddess's eye and blows himself up.

beats.headline: Reusable, if unbroken
beats.text: Carl thinks Katia should have had the credit for the goddess, since it took her bolt to do it. Katia is glad she did not: every god is angry at the one who did. Then she pulls it out of her inventory. Funny thing about magical bolts, she says: as long as they don't break, you can reuse them. Carl grins back. The princess meant it for her brother inside Grull, and that possibility is still on the table.
beats.gist: Katia pulls a reusable Bolt of Ophiotaurus from her inventory to use on the princess's brother.

beats.headline: Emberus, fifteen seconds
beats.text: Donut swaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps with the Scorpion's Bite mount on her back, cocked and loaded with Katia's bolt. She fires true, straight into Emberus's smouldering eye socket. A second shot, one of her Danforth bolts, takes the other eye and holds him in place. The yellow glow winks off: fifteen seconds, and he cannot move. Taranis, seeing his little brother rise, raises a hand and twists his wrist, and with one second left Emberus explodes.
beats.gist: Donut fires Katia's bolt into Emberus's smouldering eye socket and a Danforth bolt into the other.

recap.text: Katia receives a single crossbow bolt in a benefactor box from Princess Formidable. The bolt pauses a deity's invulnerability for fifteen seconds if it hits an eye. Carl decides the sender, the dead sister of Crown Prince Stalwart and the Maestro, is not a fan of her brother. Carl tells Katia the gift was a message rather than a plan to kill the Maestro.

Katia gives a crawler a bolt that he sticks into a goddess's eye. He blows himself up, the explosion severs her neck, and the system marks him for death by every deity except her enemies. Katia retrieves the bolt from her inventory and tells Carl it is reusable if it does not break.

Donut swaps into a room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps with a Scorpion's Bite mount on her back. She fires Katia's bolt into Emberus's smouldering eye socket and a Danforth bolt into the other eye. Taranis twists his wrist with one second left and Emberus explodes.

tagline.text: A Celestial Grenade summons its thrower's god for sixty seconds. This one was Maggie My's, bought by the Skull Empire to bring the god of pain down on Carl, and Carl dived for it and has it now.
Carl took Emberus as his god in mid-air and threw Maggie's grenade at Quan Ch. Emberus arrived, and for sixty seconds of Divine Intervention nothing could hurt Carl.

description.text: These little balls of fun were developed by the nuns of Enyo during the first enlightenment, back when the gods had to compete for worshippers. The nuns would descend upon a village and proselytize to the people about why their goddess was the best. If the villagers didn't immediately fall to their knees in veneration, the nuns would be forced to invoke a more aggressive campaign. A nun would drop a celestial grenade, which would summon Enyo directly into town for a period of sixty seconds. That was usually enough to change the minds of the survivors. Celestial grenades grant the following effects: If the wielder of the grenade has pledged themselves to a specific deity, this grenade will summon their god for sixty seconds. In addition, the wielder will receive a 60-second Divine Intervention aura. If the wielder does not worship a deity, this grenade will summon a random god. They will not receive the Divine Intervention buff.

beats.headline: The ball in the impostor's hand
beats.text: The friend standing in front of Carl is Maggie My wearing him, and she has a round, spiked ball in her hand when Katia's petrify bolt takes her in the head. The ball rolls. Carl dives for it and puts it in his inventory before it can do anything, without knowing what it is. It does not list itself as an explosive. It is a celestial grenade: summon your god for sixty seconds, and stand inside Divine Intervention while it is here.
beats.gist: Katia's petrify bolt hits Maggie My in the head, and Carl puts her spiked ball in his inventory.

beats.headline: Bought by the Skull Empire
beats.text: Mordecai's eyes go huge when Carl tosses it to him. These are very expensive and rare, he says, seen on the ninth floor a lot, near the end; using one on a single crawler is like trying to kill a bug with a kinetic strike. The crawler Maggie has been riding gets a message out before he is cut off. She worships Algos, the god of pain, chosen from a scroll sent by her sponsors, Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. She got the grenade on this floor.
beats.gist: Carl tosses a Celestial Grenade to Mordecai. Maggie's crawler sends a message before being cut off.

beats.headline: Thrown from the upper wing
beats.text: The biplane is spiralling down, Orthrus is unconscious, and Quan Ch is closing in, both hands glowing. Carl takes Emberus as his god in mid-air, against every warning in the cookbook, climbs onto the upper wing with Donut clinging to his back, and throws the grenade at Quan. Quan freezes it fifteen feet in front of him with a red bolt. It makes no difference. The ball winks out, and Emberus arrives as a city-sized floating head. Quan never gets his spell off.
beats.gist: Carl throws a Celestial Grenade at Quan from a spiralling biplane to summon Emberus as a city-sized head.

beats.headline: Sixty seconds of Divine Intervention
beats.text: The second clause is the one that saves Carl. Imbued with Divine Intervention, he is invulnerable for sixty seconds, and nothing over his head says so. He lands in a valley of the land quadrant unhurt while Donut, on his back, is knocked down to five percent. Emberus leaves early, gone with Orthrus before the minute is out. Quan Ch, who cannot see the buff, hits Carl with lightning while the buff still has a few seconds to run. Carl gets up and punches him in the face.
beats.gist: Carl uses a Celestial Grenade for sixty seconds of invulnerability and punches Quan Ch in the face.

recap.text: Katia hits Maggie My with a petrify bolt, and Carl puts a spiked ball from her hand into his inventory. Mordecai tells Carl the celestial grenade is rare and expensive. Carl throws the grenade at Quan Ch while clinging to a biplane wing, summoning Emberus as a city-sized floating head. Divine Intervention makes Carl invulnerable for sixty seconds, allowing him to survive lightning and punch Quan Ch in the face.

entities.name: Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull

tagline.text: The Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull is a wrist bracer that becomes a spiked gauntlet of orcish steel when Carl makes a fist. It warns that striking Grull's adherents may transform them into the god himself, and according to Mordecai, those adherents include horses.
Every punch Carl lands on one of Grull's adherents has a 1.5 percent chance of summoning the god. The description never said the chance was cumulative. It is.
A platinum sharpening stone has given Carl's gauntlet longer spikes, a point more strength and dexterity when he makes a fist, and a slightly oilier, meaner look.

entities.description: Item is a wrist bracer that transforms into a spiked war gauntlet made of orcish steel when the hand is shaped into a fist or wields a hilted weapon for more than two seconds at a time. This item on its own does not negate the bare knuckle skill bonus. Warning: if you use this weapon to strike adherents of the war god Grull, you have a 1.5% chance to transfigure your target into the deity himself. Trust me on this. You don't want to do that.

beats.headline: Best thing in the brawler box
beats.text: The brawler box after the gym holds exactly the weapon Carl wanted: plus three Strength in fist mode, plus one Dexterity, two levels of Iron Punch, one of Powerful Strike, a two percent chance to stun. The warning is about striking adherents of Grull. Mordecai: horses, centaurs, tikbalangs; blue makeup, wenches, dying gloriously. Grull isn't a real god, he adds; there are none here, just those who pay. A clenched fist, a two-second buzz, and the hand is a spiked black hunk of metal.
beats.gist: Carl finds the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull in the brawler box.

beats.headline: Half a snout on the fist
beats.text: First blood: a fat, tuxedoed pig knight whose health is already in the red. His face caves in under the spiked gauntlet, half of his snout stays attached to Carl's fist, and he goes down still clutching his glass of wine. Miraculously, Carl feels nothing in his hand, only the impact in his arm. That was the point: no more breaking fingers on the things he punches. The gauntlet is nothing ornate, black and angular with gleaming spikes, a tool, and it vanishes in a puff of smoke that smells of burnt hair when the fist opens.
beats.gist: Carl uses a black, angular, spiked gauntlet to cave in the face of a tuxedoed pig knight.

beats.headline: Two seconds is a long time
beats.text: A clurichaun comes at Carl impossibly fast and grapples instead of using its slingshot. He forms a fist, but the gauntlet takes two seconds to arrive, which is a long time when something is clawing at you. The first, bare-knuckle hit stuns it. The second, with the gauntlet, sends it flying with its head caved in. When he opens his hand his fingers are covered in lime-green oily residue, and a warning: he has been infected with the Taint.
beats.gist: A clurichaun grapples Carl, and the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull takes two seconds to arrive.

beats.headline: Two percent, finally
beats.text: The two percent chance to stun has never once fired. Then, in a room full of cages, a dingo's head explodes and the gerbil that was inside it rockets at Carl's throat. He was ready. One full-strength punch, and the gerbil bounces off the floor with a sickening crunch and slides into the edge of a cage, health deep in the red, Stunned over its head with a fifteen-second timer. Carl takes two steps toward the tiny, unmoving thing, with a baleful glance at the ceiling.
beats.gist: Carl punches a gerbil with the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull and stuns it.

beats.headline: It fits over the scoop
beats.text: The xistera Carl receives in the pub wraps his right forearm and retracts into a metallic bracer. While the scoop is out he can neither punch nor summon the gauntlet. Retracted, he forms a fist to test it, and the gauntlet not only works but fits snugly over the end of the new bracer, as if it had been made for it. The missing right arm of his jacket no longer looks ridiculous.
beats.gist: The Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull fits over Carl's xistera bracer.

beats.headline: It hurts ghosts
beats.text: The third floor's ghost-class mobs can only be injured by magic or magical items, and the gauntlet counts. Outside the magistrate's building it damages a swarm of stinging, cold-attacking ghosts as easily as if they were flesh; they give off an unusually high amount of experience. Inside the krasue nest, Carl punches a flying head as he rushes past, and the magical gauntlet connects with a wet splat. Mongo's magical teeth caps can hurt them too.
beats.gist: The Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull hurts ghosts and flying heads.

beats.headline: A warning from Odette
beats.text: At the end of the floor, Odette looks at Carl and tells him to be careful with that gauntlet. It has the power to summon the war god Grull if he uses it against any of Grull's celebrants, and they start appearing on the next floor. King Rust has also just spent a lot of money on a deity sponsorship, which the Skull Empire does not usually buy. She does not know which god. If she were still a gambler, she would bet on Grull.
beats.gist: Odette warns Carl the gauntlet summons the war god Grull if used against Grull's celebrants.

beats.headline: Bang Bro on the fist
beats.text: On the fourth floor Carl finds a spellbook for Bang Bro, which lets a weapon inflict Burn and Shock, and asks Mordecai whether it works on the gauntlet. Definitely, says Mordecai; not on the xistera, the way Carl loads it, but probably on his foot while his invulnerability buff is active. So Carl trains it, casting it on the gauntlet while the party grinds low-level mobs. He does not get to use it yet. The description adds that it can also cook hotdogs.
beats.gist: Carl casts a Bang Bro spell on the Grull gauntlet to inflict Burn and Shock.

beats.headline: Ten point five
beats.text: Gore-Gore, train engineer and mantaur, is an adherent of Grull. Carl punches him in the kidney and a number appears on his interface: 1.5. Four quick punches after that: 3.0, 4.5, 6.0, 7.5. The description never said it was cumulative. Two more to get away: 9.0, 10.5. Then 10.5 is blinking and Gore-Gore has a ten-second timer over his head, saying he feels it in his chest. Carl drop-kicks him onto the third rail before the god arrives.
beats.gist: Carl punches Gore-Gore in the kidney six times to trigger a ten-second timer and drop-kick him.

beats.headline: Summoning by accident
beats.text: The cookbook sorts deity summonings into three kinds, and the kind Carl's gauntlet does is the involuntary one: some poor fool summons a god by accident, through a trap or a spell or bad luck, and the god arrives angry and untethered. A second note calls it common. God-summoning equipment is sprinkled through the dungeon for special guest appearances, the deity spots are often bought by celebrities, and it is a way to collect more sponsorship money.
beats.gist: The Grull gauntlet causes involuntary deity summonings to collect sponsorship money for celebrity guests.

beats.headline: The sharpening stone
beats.text: A platinum quest box holds five thousand gold, twenty healing scrolls and a little black rock. Mordecai: this is for your gauntlet, you have to use it now. Platinum Sharpening Stone, short shelf life: rub it on a spiked weapon for bonus damage scaled to level, plus one to every existing stat buff, and a slightly oilier, meaner look. The whole gauntlet glows, the spikes grow a little longer, and the formed fist gains a point each of dexterity and strength.
beats.gist: Carl rubs a Platinum Sharpening Stone on his gauntlet for bonus damage and stat buffs.

beats.headline: A fist that does not form
beats.text: Escorted by two gnoll guards, Carl climbs a ladder into what one of them calls a zero zone, no enhancements at all, and makes a fist. For the very first time the gauntlet does not form. The guard says not to worry: studio three is a class two. The same day brings some arithmetic: past fifteen, armour and weapon enhancements like the gauntlet's plus one to Powerful Strike lose effectiveness. It still counts, with diminishing returns.
beats.gist: Carl climbs a ladder into a zero zone and the gauntlet does not form.

beats.headline: Surrendered at the door
beats.text: At the high elves' party, an elf at the twisting staircase made every guest store their weapons in inventory and then patted them down, including the wrist bracer that forms Carl's Grull gauntlet. In the melee after the queen falls, Carl grabs a mantis by the neck as he re-forms the gauntlet, and its head pops off. Another is already at his neck, then another.
beats.gist: An elf at a twisting staircase makes guests store weapons and pats down Carl's Grull gauntlet.

beats.headline: Something riding the fist
beats.text: Mid-race, with Donut chaining a tunnel of giant pasta tubes over the road, the sugar hermits surge through the gaps and a skull lands in the cab through the missing windshield. Carl punches it with the gauntlet. The skull explodes, but the purple thing that lived inside it is still attached to the metal fist, slithering octopus-like around it toward his arm. Carl casts Bang Bro and electrifies the weapon, and the creature drops off, dead and sizzling. The spell he trained on the fourth floor still earns its keep.
beats.gist: Carl punches a skull with the gauntlet, and a purple octopus-like creature attaches to the metal fist.

recap.text: Carl finds the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull in a brawler box. The black, angular metal hunk of metal caves in a tuxedoed pig knight's face, leaving half a snout on the fist. A clurichaun infects Carl with the Taint after the gauntlet takes two seconds to arrive. Carl punches a gerbil, triggering a two percent chance to stun for fifteen seconds.

Carl receives a xistera that wraps his forearm and retracts into a metallic bracer, fitting snugly over the end of the bracer. The gauntlet damages stinging, cold-attacking ghosts and a flying head with a wet splat. Odette warns that using the gauntlet against celebrants summons the war god Grull. King Rust buys a deity sponsorship, and Odette bets it is Grull.

Carl casts a spellbook for Bang Bro on his gauntlet while the party grinds low-level mobs, adding Burn, Shock, and the ability to cook hotdogs. He punches Gore-Gore in the kidney six times to reach a blinking 10.5, then drop-kicks the mantaur onto the third rail. The gauntlet performs involuntary god-summoning, a method used for celebrity guest appearances to collect sponsorship money.

A platinum quest box holds five thousand gold, twenty healing scrolls, and a Platinum Sharpening Stone. Mordecai tells Carl to rub the stone on the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull. The gauntlet glows, the spikes grow longer, and the fist gains one point of dexterity and strength.

Carl climbs a ladder into a zero zone where the Grull gauntlet does not form. A guard explains that studio three is a class two and that enhancements like the plus one to Powerful Strike lose effectiveness past fifteen. At a party, an elf at a twisting staircase makes Carl store the wrist bracer in inventory. Carl re-forms the gauntlet and pops a mantis head off.

Donut chains a tunnel of giant pasta tubes over the road while sugar hermits surge through gaps. A skull lands in the cab through the missing windshield, and Carl punches it with the gauntlet. A purple creature slithers octopus-like from the skull toward his arm. Carl casts Bang Bro to electrify the weapon, and the creature drops off dead and sizzling.

tagline.text: Hob-lobbers are round hobgoblin bombs with an eighth of the yield of a hobgoblin stick, in fused and impact-detonated versions. Pustule has only one case of the fused ones tonight.
A fused hob-lobber is the perfect size for Carl's xistera, which sends it out like a cannonball. The fuse runs six or seven seconds, so he pre-lights them to cut it short.
Hob-lobbers are Carl's staple ammunition, fused or impact-detonated, and he cuts them down at the bench to half, quarter and eighth strength for close work.
Carl makes sticky hob-lobbers as well now, but the dungeon has learned to fight back: in one room, heat lamps threaten to set a bomb off while it is still in his hand.

description.text: Hobgoblin Hob-Lobber – Fused. Type: Fragmenting Tossable. Effect: It blows shit up. A mainstay of the Hobgoblin Hob-Lobbing Lobbers, the Hob-Lobber is a stable, mostly-predictable, more practical and tactical solution to dynamite. All right? But if you toss it, make sure its wick is lit. While not guaranteed to do a premature blast, it's better than nothing, innit?

beats.headline: Round bombs, one case left
beats.text: Carl asks the hobgoblin at the Silk Road for smaller explosives, preferably ball-shaped. Pustule normally carries round bombs. Hob-lobbers. Impact-enchanted and fused, a yield of one-eighth a hobgoblin stick, or half a goblin stick. The impact ones are dangerous, and the Hob-Lobbing Lobbers use them almost exclusively: don't drop 'em. The fused ones are impact resistant and extra stable; light, then toss. She only has a case of those tonight, twenty-five for five hundred gold. The case plus two cases of goblin dynamite come to fifteen hundred; Donut talks the lot down to a thousand.
beats.gist: Carl buys twenty-five fused hob-lobbers and two cases of goblin dynamite for one thousand gold.

beats.headline: Tossed in a safe room
beats.text: Back at the pub, Carl examines one. Stability 150, fortified, and a description whose rhymes he does not rate. The round bomb is the perfect size for his new xistera. It needs its fuse lit, a minor inconvenience; the impact-triggered kind can be bought from Pustule. Thinking about what Mordecai could do with an alchemy table, Carl tosses the heavy bomb into the air and catches it. Everyone in the room, Mongo included, looks at him in horror. I worry about you sometimes, says Donut.
beats.gist: Carl examines a round Hob-Lobber bomb with stability 150 and rhymes he does not rate.

beats.headline: Out of the xistera
beats.text: Two dozen hob-lobbers, and a problem: their fuses run six or seven seconds, perfect for tossing like grenades but too long at two hundred and fifty miles an hour. In the dark, with something slow and moaning shuffling toward him, Carl pulls one of ten he pre-lit to shorten the fuse and spins it from the xistera at the dot of the city elf who cast the spell. It flies like a cannonball and sinks into a monster twenty feet short. The second is perfectly timed. There isn't even an X left.
beats.gist: Carl spins a pre-lit hob-lobber from the xistera to shorten the fuse and hits a monster.

beats.headline: Three boxes, impact-detonated
beats.text: A stop at the Silk Road with funds running low. Carl picks up three more boxes of hob-lobbers, all of them the impact-detonated version, and Pustule has brought a ten-pack of hobgoblin smoke curtains, round fused bombs that work much better than goblin smoke. Pustule is right about the curtains. That night they fill the air over the rooftops like a heavy fog.
beats.gist: Carl buys three boxes of impact-detonated hob-lobbers and Pustule brings ten hobgoblin smoke curtains.

beats.headline: The fuse as a tester
beats.text: With the bench's bomb-deconstructing skill Carl takes several fused hob-lobbers apart; the fuses themselves could be useful. At the edge of an ochre line platform he has no multimeter, so he improvises: a curved metal rod carrying a wired hob-lobber fuse, tossed onto the tracks. It blows the moment the rod bridges the main rails and the third rail, and nowhere else. The third rail is the hot one, as it should be.
beats.gist: Carl uses a bomb-deconstructing skill to take hob-lobbers apart and tosses a fuse onto tracks.

beats.headline: A game at the carnival
beats.text: A creature with a round mouth full of teeth charges down the rails, shrugging off a storm of crossbow bolts. Carl's metal ball shatters teeth. The next shot is a half-strength, impact-detonated hob-lobber, because the monster is too close for full strength; it goes into the giant mouth and takes out another tooth. There is a muffled thump. A moment after, the monster blows apart from the inside, like a water balloon filled with Beefaroni, and Donut gets no experience for it.
beats.gist: Carl uses a half-strength hob-lobber to blow apart a creature like a Beefaroni water balloon.

beats.headline: Through the mouth, rolling
beats.text: Invisible and running out of time between two cold engines in the trainyard, Carl finds the way out blocked by a Jabbering Jibber-Jabber, a minion of the Mimic Rex and nothing more than a giant mouth of needle teeth, a splitter. It doesn't see him. He pulls an impact-detonated hob-lobber and dives through the side of its open mouth like a trick poodle through a hoop, and keeps going. The Jibber-Jabber chomps down. None of the pieces get back up.
beats.gist: Carl dives through the mouth of a Jabbering Jibber-Jabber with an impact-detonated hob-lobber.

beats.headline: Quarter strength, then an eighth
beats.text: On the fifth floor Carl keeps cutting his bombs down. A quarter-strength hob-lobber lobbed over a hill at a lizard thirty feet off leaves a red geyser, and he decides it is still too strong for close combat: shrapnel. He needs something half that. By the time camels are firing rockets at a door he is holding, he has them, and coughs fire in the hole and hurls one of his new eighth-strength hob-lobbers down the long hall. The secondary explosion is bigger than the first.
beats.gist: Carl cuts the strength of his hob-lobber bombs to avoid shrapnel and hurls one at camels.

beats.headline: Seeded into death charges
beats.text: Two commentators admire Carl's depth charges on air. Multi-layered, gunpowder-filled barrels, seeded with impact-detonated hob-lobbers that go off the moment the barrel crushes under the pressure, with holes and a manual dial to choose how deep. Donut calls them death charges. While the commentators jabber and the display window is about to break, Carl yanks the fuse out of a hob-lobber and replaces it with a piece of hobgoblin pus, bought from Pustule, and burns through more of his expensive detonator materials.
beats.gist: Carl uses gunpowder-filled barrels seeded with impact-detonated hob-lobbers that Donut calls death charges.

beats.headline: Sticky, against a Santa hat
beats.text: Carl has been working on sticky bombs for a while, and took the adhesive problem into the production facility's bomber's studio on the sixth floor. In a card-game combat against a wide-faced man in a Santa hat, Carl pulls a sticky hob-lobber into his xistera and throws it across the way. It splotches against the man's chest and explodes, killing him before he draws his first card. Donut's complaint is that Carl blew up his hat.
beats.gist: Carl throws a sticky hob-lobber at a wide-faced man in a Santa hat, killing him.

beats.headline: The heat lamps
beats.text: A card duel, two lizard temple guards summoned onto the field, and Carl reaches for a hob-lobber and examines it before he throws, as he should. Warning: the current environment may cause this to explode prematurely. In fact, just holding it could be bad for your health. A five-second timer appears over it, and he puts it away fast. It is the heat lamps. They are there on purpose, designed specifically to fuck with his bombs. His weakest, a sixteenth-strength, had already gone off early.
beats.gist: Carl examines a hob-lobber during a card duel with two lizard temple guards.

beats.headline: The Shit Just Hit folder
beats.text: No time to aim. Carl levitates up out of the funnel of Larracos and, instead of placing the big waffle-maker bombs on the theatre housing the zarogoth generator, drops the entire contents of one inventory folder, labelled Shit Just Hit, in the general direction of the Piccadilly. About twenty waffle makers, two no disassembles, a pair of cheese cutters, more dynamite sticks than he can count, and approximately five hundred impact hob-lobbers, all at once. His Walk on Air runs out three-quarters of the way to safety.
beats.gist: Carl drops the contents of his Shit Just Hit folder, including five hundred impact hob-lobbers, toward the Piccadilly.

beats.headline: Trollish Boom Boxes
beats.text: On the tenth floor Carl finally starts receiving more dynamite and hob-lobbers, some surefires, which is a relief, and a Bomb Blanket potion that stops smaller bombs going off if thrown on them in time. There is also something new, Trollish Boom Boxes, which are upgraded hob-lobbers: they look like shoeboxes on a stick and are meant to be thrown. Carl wants to play with them in his bomber's studio first.
beats.gist: Carl receives dynamite, surefires, hob-lobbers, and Trollish Boom Boxes that look like shoeboxes on a stick.

recap.text: Carl buys twenty-five fused hob-lobbers and two cases of goblin dynamite from Pustule for one thousand gold. He finds the round bombs fit his xistera, though he must pre-light the fuses to shorten them for high-speed use. He buys three boxes of impact-detonated hob-lobbers and ten hobgoblin smoke curtains.

Carl uses a bench's bomb-deconstructing skill to take apart fused hob-lobbers. He tosses a metal rod with a fuse onto tracks to find the hot third rail. He shoots a half-strength hob-lobber into a creature's mouth, making it blow apart like a water balloon filled with Beefaroni. Carl dives through the open mouth of a Jabbering Jibber-Jabber with an impact-detonated hob-lobber.

Carl lobs a quarter-strength hob-lobber at a lizard thirty feet away, creating a red geyser. He cuts the strength to an eighth to avoid shrapnel and hurls one down a hall while camels fire rockets at a door. Carl builds depth charges using gunpowder-filled barrels seeded with impact-detonated hob-lobbers. He replaces a hob-lobber fuse with hobgoblin pus bought from Pustule.

Carl takes an adhesive problem to a bomber's studio on the sixth floor to make sticky bombs. He throws a sticky hob-lobber at a wide-faced man in a Santa hat, killing him before he draws a card. Heat lamps in a card duel cause a hob-lobber to show a five-second timer, as a sixteenth-strength bomb already went off early.

Carl levitates out of the funnel of Larracos. He drops the contents of an inventory folder labelled Shit Just Hit toward the Piccadilly, including twenty waffle makers, two no disassembles, two cheese cutters, many dynamite sticks, and five hundred impact hob-lobbers. His Walk on Air runs out three-quarters of the way to safety.

Carl receives dynamite, surefires, and hob-lobbers. He gets a Bomb Blanket potion to stop smaller bombs. He receives Trollish Boom Boxes, which look like shoeboxes on a stick, and wants to play with them in his bomber's studio.

entities.name: Spunky Jefferson
aka: Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock of the Elderly Miser
entities.role: Sapient nickel-sock flail · Dong Quixote's weapon

tagline.text: Spunky Jefferson is a crusty tube sock full of nickels, cursed to hold the life force of an elderly miser. It is sapient, it grows stronger as it kills, and Dong Quixote has taken it as his flail.
Dong's sock grows bigger every day, and it seems to be keeping him alive just by being near him. Imani does not like the look of that.
The sock was torn in a bar fight, shrank back to its original size, and stopped talking to Dong. Then it left him, cursed with Negative ROI, and told him he was a bad investment.

description.text: Jefferson is the life force of such a miser who pissed off the spirit who'd come to show him the errors of his ways. He was cursed to inhabit a sock once owned by a kid named Tanner. The sock itself holds several USD worth of nickels. You swing it and bonk people with it.

beats.headline: Handed over as a flail
beats.text: Dong Quixote wants a one-handed flail, and the nearest thing in Carl's inventory, looted from Quan Ch, has a description he has not read yet. Sapient. Incremental damage, currently up 238%. Mobs it kills may burst into gold. It is a white tube sock, red and blue stripes, old, crusty and bloodstained, sagging with coins. Dong takes it reverently and calls it a mythical weapon, then starts talking to it: five gold coins a dance, and no, he does not know what a mutual fund is.
beats.gist: Dong Quixote takes a sapient, bloodstained nickel-sock flail from Carl and asks it about mutual funds.

beats.headline: Uh oh. It talks.
beats.text: An achievement catches up with Carl for looting a sapient weapon. Very few well-known crawlers use them, it notes, though they are usually quite powerful. Good luck with that. The reward is a pair of earplugs. Mordecai has already warned that such things can be both annoying and dangerous. Carl has not yet heard the sock say a word, but he has an uneasy feeling about it now, and makes a note to go back and examine it more closely.
beats.gist: Carl loots Spunky Jefferson, a sapient nickel-sock flail, and receives earplugs as an achievement reward.

beats.headline: Mr. Jefferson says
beats.text: Dong keeps the nickel end near his ear, and Carl is fairly sure the thing talks to him in his mind; earlier on this floor he was heard laughing quietly with it about long-term investments and short-term gains. Back from searching the Desperado Club for two missing strippers, Dong starts relaying Mr. Jefferson's view on high-stress environments. Donut forbids him to discuss her with his disgusting sock. He said you would say that, Dong replies.
beats.gist: Dong keeps Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock of the Elderly Miser near his ear.

beats.headline: Jefferson is correct
beats.text: Dong turns up for Carl's operation on Gonk with the sock over his shoulder, pausing mid-explanation to agree with it: yes, yes, you're right, Jefferson, it is very cost effective. Then, with the enemy army away from its castle, he makes the case: he and Jefferson have been talking, and Jefferson is correct. They should make haste to the Madness castle and proceed with the plan. Carl decides to trust the others and deal with the castle in front of him.
beats.gist: Dong arrives for Carl's operation on Gonk with Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock.

beats.headline: A coin kissed and fed
beats.text: Mobs killed by the sock sometimes leave gold coins on the ground. Carl watches Dong dismount, find one still spinning, snatch it up, kiss it, open the bloody sock and drop it in with a clink. I thought they were all nickels in there, Carl says. Dong is muttering to himself and does not answer. Carl turns back to the carnage and loots the bodies.
beats.gist: Dong kisses a spinning gold coin and drops it into Spunky Jefferson.

beats.headline: Sustaining, or addicted
beats.text: Dong, sitting on his giant stinking nickel sock and muttering about IRAs, is already feeling better. Imani asks whether he had it with him outside. He did not; he left it in the garage. Her read: the other team cast nothing. The sock heals him by proximity without his health going up, which means it is sustaining him, and if he is addicted to it she does not know what to do yet. Donut says it gets bigger every day. Nobody tells Dong. They do not want the sock to panic.
beats.gist: Dong sits on Spunky Jefferson, a giant stinking nickel sock, and mutters about IRAs.

beats.headline: Torn open on the dance floor
beats.text: In the brawl during Carl and Donut's song, Dong clears the stage swinging his gigantic sock over his head. A mantis-like creature slices at him; he sends her flying, but not before she tears a hole in it. Coins fly everywhere, and every one is a nickel, though he has been putting gold pieces in. Dozens of NPCs grab handfuls and run. The tear mends itself. The sock does not go back to its giant size, however many nickels are put back in.
beats.gist: Dong swings Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock of the Elderly Miser over his head.

beats.headline: A bad investment
beats.text: The sock is back to its original size and has stopped talking to Dong. Then his health starts to dip under a debuff reading Negative ROI. Bucket Boy grabs the sock to ask it what is wrong; it attacks him and is teleported away by the safe room rules. Mordecai: it could be anywhere. Sapient weapons use their owners until they can't, then move on. Mistress Tiatha calls the curse Separation Anxiety. Dong's own account: Jefferson said I was a bad investment.
beats.gist: Spunky Jefferson tells Dong he is a bad investment and stops talking to him.

recap.text: Dong Quixote wants a one-handed flail. Carl gives him a white tube sock with red and blue stripes, old, crusty, bloodstained, and sagging with coins, looted from Quan Ch. The sapient sock has incremental damage up 238 percent and makes mobs burst into gold. Dong Quixote calls it a mythical weapon and asks it for five gold coins a dance.

Carl receives earplugs as a reward for looting a sapient weapon. Dong uses the sock, named Spunky Jefferson, to discuss investments and high-stress environments. Dong and Jefferson agree to proceed to the Madness castle. Dong kisses a gold coin from a dead mob and drops it into the bloody sock.

Dong sits on a stinking nickel sock and mutters about IRAs. During a song, Dong swings the gigantic sock to clear a stage, but a mantis-like creature tears a hole in it and nickels fly everywhere. The sock returns to its original size, stops talking to Dong, and gives him a Negative ROI debuff. The sock attacks Bucket Boy and is teleported away, leaving Dong as a bad investment.
